texts1: The New York City Fire Department (FDNY) provides fire protection, technical rescue, response to various hazards, and emergency medical services throughout the five boroughs of New York City. It is the largest municipal fire department in the United States and the second largest in the world, after the Tokyo Fire Department. The FDNY employs approximately 11,080 uniformed firefighters and over 3,300 uniformed EMTs and paramedics. The department is often referred to as New York's Bravest.

According to Italian fashion designer Roberto Cavalli, Beyoncé uses different fashion styles to complement her music during performances. A book co-written by a member of her family, published in 2002, titled Destiny's Style, provides an account of how fashion influenced the trio's success. The B'Day Anthology Video Album showcased numerous fashion-oriented scenes, featuring wardrobe styles ranging from classic to contemporary. In 2007, Beyoncé appeared on the cover of the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue, becoming the second African American woman after Tyra Banks to do so, and People magazine recognized Beyoncé as the best-dressed celebrity.

New York City is located in the Northeastern United States, in the southeastern part of New York State, roughly halfway between Washington, D.C. and Boston. Its position at the base of a major river, where the river meets a naturally sheltered harbor and then the Atlantic Ocean, has contributed to its prominence as a trading port. Most of New York City is built on three islands: Long Island, Manhattan, and Staten Island.

According to census data, New York City is home to the largest Asian community among U.S. cities. Within the city, Queens stands out as the borough with the highest Asian American population in the state. Queens is also recognized as one of the most ethnically diverse urban areas in the world. The Chinese demographic is the most rapidly expanding nationality in New York State, with several Chinatowns developing beyond the original enclave in Manhattan—these include communities in Brooklyn and the Flushing area of Queens. These neighborhoods continue to grow and extend into nearby areas. Both the New York metropolitan area and the state have become important destinations for new Chinese immigrants, with significant migration continuing in New York City and its suburbs. In 2012, individuals of Chinese descent made up a notable portion of the city’s population, with the majority residing in Queens or Brooklyn, both of which are located on Long Island. Flushing, Queens is home to a sizable Korean-Chinese (Chaoxianzu or Joseonjok) community, and New York City also hosts a large Tibetan population, with most Tibetans living in Queens. Koreans and Japanese are also represented in the city’s population, with Japanese making up a small percentage. Filipinos are the most numerous Southeast Asian group, followed by Vietnamese. Indians are the largest South Asian group, with Bangladeshis and Pakistanis also present. Queens is the preferred borough for Asian Indians, Koreans, Filipinos, Malaysians, and other Southeast Asians, while Brooklyn attracts significant numbers of both West Indian and Asian Indian immigrants.

The Hudson River flows through the Hudson Valley and eventually empties into New York Bay. The river acts as a boundary between the city and a neighboring state. The East River, a tidal strait, connects to Long Island Sound and separates the Bronx and Manhattan from Long Island. The Harlem River, also a tidal strait, runs between the Hudson and East Rivers and divides most of Manhattan from the Bronx. The Bronx River, which passes through the Bronx and Westchester County, is the only river in the city that is entirely fresh water.

Lee's childhood friend, author Truman Capote, praised her first novel on its dust jacket, describing it as the work of a rare and talented writer with a lively sense of life and humor. Over time, some have speculated that Capote was more involved in the writing process than acknowledged. In 2003, a Tuscaloosa newspaper quoted Capote's biological father, Archulus Persons, as claiming that Capote had written "almost all" of the book. In 2006, a letter from Capote was donated to a literary heritage museum; in it, he mentioned that Lee was working on a book that would be published soon. Extensive correspondence between Lee and her editor also challenges the rumor of Capote's authorship. Lee's older sister, Alice, strongly denied the speculation.

Starting in 2007, several major airlines reached agreements to install iPod seat connections. This service enables passengers to power and charge an iPod, as well as access their video and music libraries through individual seat-back displays. KLM and Air France were initially mentioned as potential participants, but later clarified that they were only considering the option and did not join the agreement at that time.

In soccer, New York City is represented by New York City FC of Major League Soccer, who play their home games at Yankee Stadium. The New York Red Bulls are based in nearby Harrison, New Jersey. Historically, the city is known for the New York Cosmos, the highly successful former professional soccer team which was the American home of Pelé, one of the world's most famous soccer players. A new version of the New York Cosmos was formed in 2010, and began play in the second division North American Soccer League in 2013. The Cosmos play their home games at James M. Shuart Stadium, located on the campus of Hofstra University.

In 1785, New York became the national capital shortly after the war. New York was the last capital of the U.S. under the Articles of Confederation and the first capital under the Constitution of the United States. In 1789, the first President of the United States, George Washington, was inaugurated; the first United States Congress and the Supreme Court of the United States each assembled for the first time, and the United States Bill of Rights was drafted, all at Federal Hall. By 1790, New York had surpassed Philadelphia as the largest city in the United States.

The Battle of Long Island, a major engagement of the American Revolutionary War, took place entirely within the modern-day borough of Brooklyn. After the Americans were defeated in this battle, a series of smaller armed engagements followed. The city subsequently became the British military and political base of operations in North America. It served as a haven for Loyalist refugees, as well as escaped slaves who joined the British lines in pursuit of freedom promised by the Crown to those who fought for them. When the British forces evacuated at the close of the war in 1783, they transported many freedmen for resettlement in Nova Scotia, England, and the Caribbean.

A rescue team reported survivors from the town of Yingxiu in Wenchuan County, which had a population of about 9,000. In Beichuan County, Sichuan, thousands of people were killed, with 10,000 injured and 80% of the buildings destroyed. The old county seat of Beichuan was abandoned and preserved as part of the Beichuan Earthquake Museum. Several schools collapsed in Dujiangyan. During a rescue attempt on the Lingyanshan Ropeway in Dujiangyan, a 56-year-old lost their life, and 11 tourists from Taiwan were trapped inside cable cars since May 13 due to the earthquake. In Mianzhu City, a 4-year-old boy named Zhu Shaowei (traditional Chinese: 朱紹維; simplified Chinese: 朱绍维; pinyin: Zhū Shàowéi) was killed when a house collapsed on him, and another person was reported missing.

After graduating from high school, West received a scholarship to attend Chicago's American Academy of Art in 1997 and began taking painting classes, but shortly after transferred to Chicago State University to study English. He soon realized that his busy class schedule was detrimental to his musical work, and at 20 he dropped out of college to pursue his musical dreams. This action greatly displeased his mother, who was also a professor at the university. She later commented, "It was drummed into my head that college is the ticket to a good life... but some career goals don't require college. For Kanye to make an album called College Dropout it was more about having the guts to embrace who you are, rather than following the path society has carved out for you."

Several important historic sites are located in and around New York Harbor. The Statue of Liberty National Monument and the Ellis Island Immigration Museum are found in both New York and New Jersey. These sites share the harbor with Governors Island National Monument, which is in New York. On Manhattan Island, there are a number of federally administered historic locations, including Castle Clinton National Monument, Federal Hall National Memorial, Theodore Roosevelt Birthplace National Historic Site, General Grant National Memorial—commonly known as "Grant's Tomb"—African Burial Ground National Monument, and Hamilton Grange National Memorial. Additionally, many privately owned sites are recognized on the National Register of Historic Places or as National Historic Landmarks. Among these is the Stonewall Inn in Greenwich Village, widely regarded as the birthplace of the modern LGBT rights movement.

Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts, anchoring Lincoln Square on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, is a major cultural hub. The Lee Strasberg Theatre and Film Institute is in Union Square, and Tisch School of the Arts is based at New York University, while Central Park SummerStage presents performances of free plays and music in Central Park.

New York City is home to the Major League Soccer team New York City FC, which hosts its matches at Yankee Stadium. The New York Red Bulls, meanwhile, are based in Harrison, New Jersey. In the past, New York was also recognized for the New York Cosmos, a prominent professional soccer club that famously featured Pelé, one of the sport’s greatest icons. The Cosmos were reestablished in 2010 and started competing in a professional soccer league in 2013. Their home games are held at James M. Shuart Stadium, located on the Hofstra University campus.

During the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period of China (907–960), while the fractured political realm of China saw no threat in a Tibet which was in just as much political disarray, there was little in the way of Sino-Tibetan relations. Few documents involving Sino-Tibetan contacts survive from the Song dynasty (960–1279). The Song were far more concerned with countering northern enemy states of the Khitan-ruled Liao dynasty (907–1125) and Jurchen-ruled Jin dynasty (1115–1234).

The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess (Japanese: ゼルダの伝説 トワイライトプリンセス, Hepburn: Zeruda no Densetsu: Towairaito Purinsesu) was developed and published by Nintendo for the GameCube and Wii consoles. As part of the Legend of Zelda franchise, the game’s release was delayed by Nintendo to improve the experience and to prepare a version for the Wii system. The Wii edition was released in North America in November 2006, coinciding with the launch of the console, and the GameCube version became available worldwide in December 2006.

The narrative centers around the main character as he strives to save Hyrule from being consumed by a dark parallel world called the Twilight Realm. Throughout his journey, he transforms between his usual form and that of a wolf, receiving guidance and support from a mysterious being named Midna. This storyline unfolds several centuries after certain earlier events and exists in a separate timeline from The Wind Waker.

To Kill a Mockingbird is a novel published in 1960. It was immediately successful, winning the Pulitzer Prize, and has become a classic of modern American literature. The plot and characters are loosely based on the author's observations of family and neighbors, as well as on an event that occurred near the author's hometown in 1936, when the author was 10 years old.

New York City has played a major role in shaping various cultural movements, such as the Harlem Renaissance and abstract expressionism, which is also known as the New York School. The city is recognized for its influence in music, fashion, and the arts. It serves as a prominent setting in popular culture, appearing in numerous books, films, and television series. One of the most significant fashion events held there is New York Fashion Week, which attracts considerable media coverage. The Global Language Monitor has frequently ranked New York as the leading fashion capital of the world in its annual reports.

In December, Beyoncé, along with various other celebrities, participated in a video campaign for "Demand A Plan," a bipartisan initiative by a group of 950 US mayors and others aimed at encouraging the federal government to reconsider its gun control laws after a major national tragedy. Beyoncé also became an ambassador for the 2012 World Humanitarian Day campaign, contributing a song and its music video, which was filmed at the UN, to support the cause. In 2013, it was announced that Beyoncé would collaborate with Salma Hayek and Frida Giannini on Gucci's "Chime for Change" campaign, which focuses on promoting female empowerment. The campaign, which aired on February 28, featured her new music. A concert supporting this cause took place on June 1, 2013, in London and included performances by other artists such as Ellie Goulding, Florence and the Machine, and Rita Ora. Prior to the concert, she appeared in a campaign video released on May 15, 2013, alongside Cameron Diaz, John Legend, and Kylie Minogue, where they discussed inspiration from women in their lives. Other artists also shared stories of personal inspiration, encouraging viewers to submit photos of women who inspired them, with selected images displayed at the concert. With the help of the crowdfunding platform Catapult, concert attendees could support various projects promoting education for women and girls. Beyoncé is also involved in "Miss a Meal," a food-donation campaign, and supports Goodwill through online charity auctions at Charitybuzz, which help fund job creation in Europe and the U.S.

While West had encountered controversy a year prior when he stormed out of the American Music Awards of 2004 after losing in the Best New Artist category, the rapper's first large-scale controversy came just days following Late Registration's release, during a benefit concert for Hurricane Katrina victims. In September 2005, West was a featured speaker at a televised relief event. When West was presenting alongside actor Mike Myers, he deviated from the prepared script. Myers spoke next and continued to read the script. Once it was West's turn to speak again, he made a highly publicized comment about President George Bush, which reached much of the United States and led to mixed reactions; President Bush would later call it one of the most "disgusting moments" of his presidency. West raised further controversy in January 2006 when he posed on the cover of Rolling Stone wearing a crown of thorns.

Frédéric François Chopin, born Fryderyk Franciszek Chopin, was a composer and virtuoso pianist of the Romantic era, known for his Polish and French heritage. He wrote primarily for solo piano and is celebrated worldwide as one of the leading musicians of his time, admired for his poetic genius and unmatched professional technique. Chopin was born in the Duchy of Warsaw and spent his early years there, completing his musical education and composing his initial works before departing Poland at the age of 20, shortly before a significant historical uprising.

On September 17, 2011, demonstrations known as Occupy Wall Street began in Zuccotti Park, situated in the Financial District of Manhattan. These protests drew widespread attention and sparked a movement addressing issues of social and economic inequality.

The largest engagement of the American Revolutionary War, known as the Battle of Long Island, took place entirely within what is now Brooklyn. Following the American defeat in this battle, several smaller skirmishes ensued, and New York City became the central military and political headquarters for the British in North America. During the British occupation, the city served as a refuge for Loyalists and also attracted escaped slaves, who were drawn by the British promise of freedom to those who fought for their cause. When the Revolutionary War concluded and the British army began to withdraw and evacuate the city, they relocated some freed individuals to Nova Scotia, while others were resettled in England and the Caribbean.

As of 2011, the largest sources of foreign-born individuals in the city included countries such as the Dominican Republic and China, among others. The Bangladeshi immigrant population has since become one of the fastest growing in the city, with over 74,000 residents by 2013.

The Staten Island Ferry operates the most heavily used ferry route in the world, carrying millions of people each year along its 8.4-kilometer journey between Staten Island and another borough in New York City. This service runs continuously, providing transportation 24 hours a day. Additionally, other ferry lines connect Manhattan with various destinations throughout the city and the greater metropolitan region.

From the fifth-generation iPod onward, Apple introduced a user-configurable volume limit in response to concerns about hearing loss. Users report that in the sixth-generation iPod, the maximum volume output level is limited to 100 dB in EU markets. Apple previously had to remove iPods from shelves in a country due to exceeding this legal limit. However, users who purchased a new sixth-generation iPod in late 2013 have reported a new option that allowed them to disable the EU volume limit. It has been said that these new iPods came with updated software enabling this change. Older sixth-generation iPods, however, are unable to update to this software version.

Various accessories were developed to enhance the iPod’s ability to play music, videos, and photos. While Apple produced a limited number of these accessories—including the iPod Hi-Fi, which is no longer available—most are created by third-party companies such as Belkin and Griffin. Some peripherals operate independently, while others make use of the iPod’s display. Because a proprietary technology is involved, third-party manufacturers must pay royalties to Apple in order to create compatible accessories.

Unlike other major American cities, New York is uniquely split between two primary US district courts, each with its own main courthouse located in a different borough. The Southern District of New York’s main courthouse is situated on Foley Square in Manhattan, and it oversees cases from multiple areas. Meanwhile, the Eastern District of New York’s main courthouse is found in Brooklyn, with its jurisdiction including several boroughs such as Staten Island. Additionally, New York is home to the US Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit and the US Court of International Trade, both of which are also located on Foley Square in Manhattan. iPods have faced criticism regarding their supposedly limited lifespan and the vulnerability of their hard drives. In 2005, the MacInTouch website carried out a survey to determine how frequently iPods failed. Their findings showed an average failure rate of 13.7% across the iPod range, though they acknowledged that feedback from participants suggested the actual failure rate might be somewhat lower. The survey also revealed that certain models were sturdier than others; specifically, iPods equipped with hard drives had failure rates typically exceeding 20%, whereas those using flash memory experienced failure rates under 10%. Towards the end of 2005, a significant number of first generation iPod Nano owners reported that the device’s surface was prone to scratching, which could make the screen unreadable. This led to a class action lawsuit. Although Apple initially downplayed the issue as a minor flaw, the company eventually began including protective sleeves with these iPods to address the problem.

Spectre was released on 26 October 2015 in the United Kingdom, followed by a worldwide release. It was released in the United States on 6 November 2015. It became the second James Bond film to be screened in IMAX venues after Skyfall, although it was not filmed with IMAX cameras. Spectre received mixed reviews upon its release; although criticised for its length, lack of screen time for new characters, and writing, it received praise for its action sequences and cinematography. The theme song, "Writing's on the Wall", received mixed reviews, particularly compared to the previous theme; it also received major music awards recognition. As of 20 February 2016, Spectre has grossed over $879 million worldwide.

In 1827, soon after the death of Chopin's youngest sister Emilia, the family moved from the Warsaw University building, adjacent to the Kazimierz Palace, to lodgings just across the street from the university, in the south annex of the Krasiński Palace on Krakowskie Przedmieście, where Chopin lived until he left Warsaw in 1830. Here his parents continued running their boarding house for male students; the Chopin Family Parlour (Salonik Chopinów) became a museum in the 20th century. In 1829, a set of portraits of Chopin family members was created, including the first known portrait of the composer.

As of 2011, the largest group of foreign-born individuals came from the Dominican Republic, with China as the second largest source. Other significant countries of origin included several nations in the Americas, the Caribbean, and Asia. By 2013, the number of immigrants from Bangladesh had grown rapidly, reaching over 74,000 people living in the city.

The city's fashion industry generates about $11 billion in annual wages for its workforce.

New York is also a major center for non-commercial educational media. The oldest public-access television channel in the United States is the Manhattan Neighborhood Network, founded in 1971. WNYC, a public radio station owned by the city until 1997, has the largest public radio audience in the United States.

By 1700, the Lenape population had diminished to 200.

At the upper boundary of the atmosphere, Earth is exposed to 174,000 terawatts (TW) of solar energy. Roughly 30% of this incoming radiation is reflected back into space by the atmosphere. The remaining portion is absorbed by the planet’s clouds, oceans, and land surfaces. The sunlight that reaches the Earth's surface is primarily distributed within the visible and near-infrared wavelengths, with a smaller fraction in the near-ultraviolet range. In most inhabited regions, daily solar energy received typically ranges from 150 to 300 watts per square meter, which is equivalent to about 3.5 to 7.0 kilowatt-hours per square meter per day.

In mid-2015, a new model of the iPod Touch was announced by Apple and was officially released on the Apple store on July 15, 2015. This latest iPod Touch features a variety of spec improvements, including the upgraded A8 processor and a higher-quality screen. The core is over 5 times faster than previous models and is built to be roughly on par with the iPhone 5S. It is available in 5 different colors: Space grey, pink, gold, silver, and Product (red).

The city's total area is 468.9 square miles (1,214 km²). Of this, 164.1 square miles (425 km²) is water. The highest point in the city is Todt Hill on Staten Island, which rises to 409.8 feet (124.9 m) above sea level and is the highest point on the Eastern Seaboard south of Maine. The summit of the ridge is mostly covered in woodlands as part of the Staten Island Greenbelt.

Situated on a major natural harbor, New York City consists of five boroughs, each functioning as its own county within New York State. These boroughs—Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx, and Staten Island—make up the city as a unified municipality. Census estimates from the mid-2010s indicate that New York City had a population of over 8 million people living within an area of just 305 square miles (790 km²), making it the most densely populated major city in the United States. Residents of New York speak up to 800 different languages, making it the most linguistically diverse city in the world. The metropolitan area surrounding New York City remains the largest in the country, with a Combined Statistical Area population of over 23 million. In terms of economic output, the region’s gross metropolitan product ranks first in the nation and is comparable to the economies of some of the world’s largest countries.

Go Set a Watchman, an earlier version of To Kill a Mockingbird, was released to the public amid controversy in mid-July 2015. This manuscript, completed several years before Mockingbird, is set long after the events of that novel, though it does not serve as a direct sequel. The story follows an adult Jean Louise “Scout” Finch, who returns from New York to visit her father, Atticus Finch, in Maycomb, Alabama, where she confronts the prejudice present in her hometown. The manuscript for Watchman was thought to be lost until it was reportedly found by Harper Lee’s attorney, Tonja Carter, a claim that has been the subject of much debate. Watchman features early incarnations of several characters later seen in To Kill a Mockingbird. Lee’s agent, Andrew Nurnberg, stated that Mockingbird was initially meant to be the first in a trilogy, with Watchman as the final installment and a shorter novel to connect them; however, this idea has been challenged by rare books specialist James S. Jaffe. After examining the manuscript for Lee’s lawyer, Jaffe determined that Watchman is simply another draft of To Kill a Mockingbird. Similarly, Jonathan Mahler described Watchman as merely the initial draft of Mockingbird, and the significant overlap between the texts, sometimes even identical passages, further undermines the trilogy claim.

Frédéric’s father relocated to Poland in 1787 at the age of sixteen. Starting in 1236, the Mongol prince Kublai, who later ruled as Khagan from 1260–1294, was granted a large appanage in North China by his superior, Ögedei Khan. During the years immediately following the novel's publication, Harper Lee enjoyed the attention its popularity brought her, granting interviews, visiting schools, and attending events honoring the book. When To Kill a Mockingbird was in its 41st week on the bestseller list, it was awarded a major literary prize, which stunned Lee. That same year, it also received the Brotherhood Award of the National Conference of Christians and Jews, and the following year, the Paperback of the Year award from Bestsellers magazine. Starting in 1964, Lee began to turn down interviews, expressing that the questions had become monotonous, and she grew concerned that the attention she received was similar to the publicity sought by celebrities. From that point on, she declined to speak with reporters about the book. She also steadfastly refused to provide an introduction, writing in 1995: "Introductions inhibit pleasure, they kill the joy of anticipation, they frustrate curiosity. The only good thing about Introductions is that in some cases they delay the dose to come. Mockingbird still says what it has to say; it has managed to survive the years without preamble."

The Hudson River runs through the Hudson Valley and empties into New York Bay. From New York City up to Troy, New York, it functions as an estuary. This river forms the boundary between New York City and the state of New Jersey. The East River, a tidal strait, connects Long Island Sound to the Upper New York Bay and divides the Bronx and Manhattan from Long Island. Another tidal strait in the area links the Hudson and East Rivers. The Bronx River, which passes through both the Bronx and Westchester County, is the city’s only purely freshwater river.

The Earth receives 174,000 terawatts (TW) of incoming solar radiation (insolation) at the upper atmosphere. A portion of this energy is reflected back to space, while the remainder is absorbed by clouds, oceans, and land masses. The spectrum of solar light at the Earth's surface is mostly spread across the visible and near-infrared ranges with a small part in the near-ultraviolet. Most people around the world live in areas that typically receive between 3.5 to 7.0 kWh/m2 per day.

As of 2014, New York City had an estimated population of 8,491,079, marking a record high. The city’s population is more than double that of the next largest city in the country, despite New York City occupying a smaller geographic area. Approximately 40% of New York State’s residents live in New York City, and the city’s population also represents a similar proportion of the total population in the New York metropolitan region.

According to census data, New York City is home to the largest Asian community among U.S. cities. Within the city, Queens stands out as the borough with the most substantial Asian American population in the state. Queens is also recognized as one of the most ethnically diverse urban areas in the world. The Chinese demographic is the most rapidly expanding nationality in New York State, with several Chinatowns developing beyond the original enclave in Manhattan, including notable communities in Brooklyn and the Flushing area of Queens. These neighborhoods continue to grow, extending into nearby areas outside the city. Both the New York metropolitan area and the state have become primary destinations for new Chinese immigrants, and significant Chinese migration continues in New York City and its suburbs. As of 2012, individuals of Chinese descent made up a notable portion of the city’s population, with the majority residing in Queens or Brooklyn, both located on Long Island. Flushing, Queens is home to a significant Korean-Chinese (Chaoxianzu or Joseonjok) community, and New York City also hosts a large Tibetan population, with most Tibetans living in Queens. Koreans and Japanese are also present in the city, with Japanese making up a small percentage of the population. Filipinos are the most numerous Southeast Asian group, followed by Vietnamese. Indians are the largest South Asian group, with Bangladeshis and Pakistanis also represented. Queens is the favored borough for Asian Indians, Koreans, Filipinos, Malaysians, and other Southeast Asians, while Brooklyn is attracting significant numbers of both West Indian and Asian Indian immigrants.

An earlier version of To Kill a Mockingbird was completed in 1957. The story is set about twenty years after the events of To Kill a Mockingbird, focusing on Jean Louise “Scout” Finch as an adult. She returns from New York to visit her father, Atticus Finch, in Maycomb, Alabama, where she faces the prejudice in her hometown. The manuscript was believed lost until it was reportedly discovered by Harper Lee’s attorney, Tonja Carter, though this account has been debated. This version features early forms of several characters later seen in To Kill a Mockingbird. Lee’s agent, Andrew Nurnberg, claimed that Mockingbird was intended as the first in a trilogy, with this manuscript as the final installment and a shorter novel to connect them; however, rare books specialist James S. Jaffe has challenged this, concluding after examining the manuscript for Lee’s lawyer that it is simply another draft of To Kill a Mockingbird. Jonathan Mahler similarly described it as the initial draft, noting significant overlap and even identical passages between the texts, which further questions the trilogy idea.

Manhattan Island is linked to New York City's outer boroughs and New Jersey by several tunnels. The Queens-Midtown Tunnel, built to relieve congestion on the bridges connecting Manhattan with Queens and Brooklyn, was the largest non-federal project in its time when it was completed in 1940. After a buffer overflow flaw was identified in the Wii edition of Twilight Princess, hackers created an exploit called the "Twilight Hack." This code could include applications and programs in the Executable and Linkable Format (ELF), as well as other homebrew software for the Wii. The Wii Menu versions 3.3 and 3.4 blocked the transfer of these exploited save files to the console, though workarounds were eventually found. The largest engagement of the American Revolutionary War, called the Battle of Long Island, occurred entirely within what is now Brooklyn during August 1776. During the British occupation, the city became a refuge for Loyalists and also attracted escaped slaves, who were drawn by British promises of freedom to those who supported their cause. At the height of this period, up to 10,000 escaped slaves sought shelter in New York. When the Revolutionary War ended in 1783 and the British army began to withdraw and evacuate the city, many freed individuals were relocated to other places, including Nova Scotia, England, and the Caribbean.

Both the New York metropolitan area and the state have become primary destinations for new Chinese immigrants, and significant Chinese migration continues in New York City and its suburbs. As of 2012, individuals of Chinese descent made up a notable portion of the city’s population, with the majority residing in Queens or Brooklyn, both located on Long Island. Flushing, Queens is home to a significant Korean-Chinese (Chaoxianzu or Joseonjok) community, and New York City also hosts a large Tibetan population, with most Tibetans living in Queens. Koreans and Japanese are also present in the city, with Japanese making up a small percentage of the population. Filipinos are the most numerous Southeast Asian group, followed by Vietnamese. Indians are the largest South Asian group, with Bangladeshis and Pakistanis also represented. Queens is the favored borough for Asian Indians, Koreans, Filipinos, Malaysians, and other Southeast Asians, while Brooklyn is attracting significant numbers of both West Indian and Asian Indian immigrants.

New York City has played a major role in shaping various cultural movements, including the Harlem Renaissance and abstract expressionism, which is also known as the New York School. The city has also contributed to the development of several music genres. It is widely regarded as a major center for dance. New York frequently appears in popular culture as the setting for numerous books, films, and television series. One of the most notable fashion events held there is New York Fashion Week, which attracts significant media coverage. The Global Language Monitor has repeatedly recognized New York in its annual reports related to fashion.

Beginning in 1236, the Mongol prince Kublai—who would later become Khagan and rule from 1260 to 1294—received a substantial appanage in northern China from his overlord. Karma Pakshi, who was the second Karmapa Lama and the leader of the Karma Kagyu school of Tibetan Buddhism, declined Kublai’s invitation. As a result, Kublai turned to Drogön Chögyal Phagpa, inviting him to his court. Kublai established a distinctive partnership with Phagpa, whereby Kublai was acknowledged as the supreme authority in political matters, while Phagpa served as his chief religious advisor. Furthermore, Kublai appointed Drogön Chögyal Phagpa as the head of the Bureau of Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs and as the priest-king of Tibet, which at that time consisted of thirteen states governed by myriarchies.

Italian designer Roberto Cavalli has noted that Beyoncé incorporates a variety of fashion styles to complement her music during performances. Her mother collaborated on a book released in 2002 called Destiny's Style, which details the influence of fashion on the group's achievements. The B'Day Anthology Video Album includes numerous scenes focused on fashion, highlighting both traditional and modern clothing choices. In 2007, Beyoncé appeared on the cover of a major swimsuit magazine, making her the second African American woman to do so, following Tyra Banks. Additionally, she has been recognized for her sense of style by various publications.

New York is the most important source of political fundraising in the United States, as four of the top five ZIP codes in the nation for political contributions are located in Manhattan. The leading ZIP code, 10021, generated the most money for the 2004 presidential campaigns of both major candidates. The city has a strong imbalance of payments with the national and state governments. It receives 83 cents in services for every $1 it sends to the federal government in taxes, meaning it annually sends $11.4 billion more than it receives back. The city also sends an additional $11 billion more each year to the state government than it receives in return.

Gateway National Recreation Area contains over 26,000 acres (10,521.83 ha) in total, most of it surrounded by New York City, including the Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge in Brooklyn and Queens, which covers over 9,000 acres (36 km²) of salt marsh, islands, and water, including most of Jamaica Bay. Also in Queens, the park includes a significant portion of the western Rockaway Peninsula, most notably Jacob Riis Park. In Staten Island, the park includes historic sites and recreational areas such as Fort Wadsworth, with pre-Civil War era structures, and Great Kills Park, which features beaches, trails, and a marina.

In soccer, New York City is represented by New York City FC of Major League Soccer, who play their home games at Yankee Stadium. The New York Red Bulls are based in nearby Harrison, New Jersey. Historically, the city is known for the New York Cosmos, the highly successful former professional soccer team which was the American home of Pelé, one of the world's most famous soccer players. A new version of the New York Cosmos was formed in 2010, and began play in the second division North American Soccer League in 2013. The Cosmos play their home games at James M. Shuart Stadium, located on the campus of Hofstra University.

Major tourist destinations include Times Square; Broadway theater productions; the Empire State Building; the Statue of Liberty; Ellis Island; the United Nations Headquarters; museums such as the Metropolitan Museum of Art; greenspaces such as Central Park and Washington Square Park; Rockefeller Center; Chinatown in Manhattan; luxury shopping along major avenues; and events such as the Halloween Parade in Greenwich Village; the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade; the lighting of the Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree; the St. Patrick's Day parade; seasonal activities such as ice skating in Central Park in the wintertime; the Tribeca Film Festival; and free performances in Central Park at Summerstage. Major attractions in the boroughs outside Manhattan include Flushing Meadows-Corona Park and the Unisphere in Queens; the Bronx Zoo; Coney Island in Brooklyn; and the New York Botanical Garden in the Bronx. A large ferris wheel was under construction at the northern shore of Staten Island in 2015, overlooking the harbor and city skyline.

New York—often referred to as New York City or the City of New York to distinguish it from the State of New York, of which it is a part—is the most populous city in the United States and the center of the New York metropolitan area, ranking among the largest urban agglomerations in the world. A global power city, New York exerts a significant impact upon commerce, finance, media, art, fashion, research, technology, education, and entertainment, its fast pace defining the term New York minute. Home to the headquarters of the United Nations, New York is an important center for international diplomacy and has been described as the cultural and financial capital of the world.

After graduating from high school, West received a scholarship in 1997 and began taking painting classes, but shortly after transferred to Chicago State University to study English. He soon realized that his busy class schedule was detrimental to his musical work, and at 20 he dropped out of college to pursue his musical dreams. This action greatly displeased his mother, who was also a professor at the university. She later commented, "It was drummed into my head that college is the ticket to a good life... but some career goals don't require college. For Kanye to make an album called College Dropout it was more about having the guts to embrace who you are, rather than following the path society has carved out for you."

Commercial solar water heaters began appearing in the United States in the 1890s. These systems saw increasing use until the 1920s but were gradually replaced by cheaper and more reliable heating fuels. As with photovoltaics, solar water heating attracted renewed attention as a result of the oil crises in the 1970s but interest subsided in the 1980s due to falling petroleum prices. Development in the solar water heating sector progressed steadily throughout the 1990s and growth rates have averaged 20% per year since 1999. Although generally underestimated, solar water heating and cooling is by far the most widely deployed solar technology.

The dock connector enabled the iPod to connect to various accessories, which could enhance its music, video, and photo playback features. While Apple offered some accessories, most were produced by third-party companies such as Belkin and Griffin. Some peripherals use their own interface, while others interact directly with the iPod's screen. Since the dock connector is a proprietary interface, third parties must pay royalties to Apple to implement it.

Approximately 37% of the city's population is foreign born. In New York, no single country or region of origin dominates. As of 2011, the largest sources of foreign-born individuals in the city included countries such as the Dominican Republic and China. The Bangladeshi immigrant population has since become one of the fastest growing in the city, with over 74,000 residents by 2013.

In December, Beyoncé joined numerous other celebrities to create a video campaign for "Demand A Plan," a bipartisan initiative backed by 950 U.S. mayors and additional supporters. This campaign aimed to persuade the federal government to reconsider its gun control policies in the aftermath of the Sandy Hook Elementary School tragedy. As part of the 2012 World Humanitarian Day campaign, Beyoncé served as an ambassador and contributed a song, along with its music video, which was filmed at the United Nations. In 2013, it was revealed that Beyoncé would collaborate with others on Gucci’s "Chime for Change" campaign, which focuses on advancing female empowerment. The campaign, which premiered on February 28, featured her latest music. A benefit concert supporting this cause was held in London on June 1, 2013, and included performances by artists such as Ellie Goulding, Florence and the Machine, and Rita Ora. Prior to the event, Beyoncé appeared in a promotional video released on May 15, 2013, where she and other celebrities spoke about the inspiration they drew from their mothers. Other artists highlighted the influence of significant women in their lives, and viewers were encouraged to submit photos of women who inspired them, some of which were showcased during the concert. Speaking about her mother, Beyoncé remarked on a special talent for "finding the best qualities in every human being," though she did not specify whom she was referring to. Through the use of the crowdfunding platform Catapult, concert attendees were able to support various projects aimed at promoting education for women and girls. Additionally, Beyoncé is involved in the "Miss a Meal" food donation initiative and supports the Goodwill charity by participating in online auctions through Charitybuzz, which help create jobs across Europe and the United States.

The FDNY headquarters is located in Downtown Brooklyn, and the FDNY Fire Academy is situated on Randalls Island. There are three Bureau of Fire Communications alarm offices that receive and dispatch alarms to appropriate units. One office in Brooklyn houses Manhattan/Citywide, Brooklyn, and Staten Island Fire Communications, while the Bronx and Queens offices are in separate buildings.

About 37% of New York City’s residents were born outside the United States. The city’s immigrant population is highly diverse, with no single country or region making up a majority. As of 2011, the Dominican Republic was the largest source of foreign-born individuals, with China as the second largest. Other significant countries of origin included several from Latin America, the Caribbean, South Asia, and Eastern Europe. By 2013, the number of immigrants from Bangladesh had grown rapidly, with more than 74,000 people from that country living in the city.

West demonstrated an affinity for the arts at an early age; he began writing poetry when he was five years old. His mother recalled that she first took notice of West's passion for drawing and music when he was in the third grade. Growing up in the city, West became deeply involved in its hip hop scene. He started rapping in the third grade and began making musical compositions in the seventh grade, eventually selling them to other artists. At age thirteen, West wrote a rap song called "Green Eggs and Ham" and began to persuade his mother to pay $25 an hour for time in a recording studio. It was a small, crude basement studio where a microphone hung from the ceiling by a wire clothes hanger. Although this wasn't what West's mother wanted, she nonetheless supported him. Early in his career, West crossed paths with a producer and DJ who quickly became a close friend and mentor. From this mentor, West learned how to sample and program beats after he received his first sampler at age 15.

In 2013, Omnicom Group and Interpublic Group, two of the world’s largest advertising agencies headquartered in Manhattan, together generated about US$21 billion in annual revenue. This underscores New York City’s status as the leading global hub for the advertising sector, commonly known as "Madison Avenue." The fashion industry in New York City employs around 180,000 people and pays out roughly $11 billion in wages each year.

The score for Spectre was created during the filming process, rather than after filming had ended. The theatrical trailer, released in July 2015, featured a version of John Barry's On Her Majesty's Secret Service theme. According to Mendes, the completed film included over one hundred minutes of music. The soundtrack album became available for purchase in the UK on 23 October 2015 and in the USA on 6 November 2015, released by Decca Records.

New York is also a major center for non-commercial educational media. The oldest public-access television channel in the United States is the Manhattan Neighborhood Network, founded in 1971. WNYC, a public radio station, has the largest public radio audience in New York.

During the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period of China (907–960), there was little interaction between China and Tibet. Few records of contacts between the two regions exist from the Song dynasty (960–1279). During this time, the Song focused on addressing threats from northern states, including the Liao dynasty (907–1125) and the Jin dynasty (1115–1234).

Beginning in mid-2007, several major airlines became the first to sign agreements to equip their aircraft with seat connections compatible with iPods. This complimentary service allows travelers to charge their iPods and access their music and video collections directly through the personal seat-back screens. Initially, some other airlines were mentioned as potential partners in Apple’s initiative, but later clarified that they were only considering the addition of these features and had not committed to the 2007 agreement.

Manhattan Island is linked to New York City’s outer boroughs and New Jersey by several major tunnels. One tunnel beneath the Hudson River between Midtown Manhattan and New Jersey is the world’s busiest vehicular tunnel, accommodating 120,000 vehicles each day. A tunnel was chosen over a bridge at this location to allow large passenger and cargo ships to continue traveling through New York Harbor and up the Hudson River to Manhattan’s docks. The Holland Tunnel, which connects Lower Manhattan with Jersey City, New Jersey, became the first vehicular tunnel to use mechanical ventilation when it opened in 1927. To help ease traffic on the bridges connecting Manhattan with Queens and Brooklyn, the Queens-Midtown Tunnel was constructed and, upon its completion in 1940, was the largest project of its kind not funded by the federal government. President Franklin D. Roosevelt was the inaugural driver through the Queens-Midtown Tunnel. Additionally, the Hugh L. Carey Tunnel runs beneath Battery Park, joining the Financial District at Manhattan’s southern end to Red Hook in Brooklyn.

The Statue of Liberty National Monument and Ellis Island Immigration Museum are managed together and are located in both New York and another neighboring state. They are joined in the harbor by Governors Island National Monument, which is in New York. Historic sites under federal management on Manhattan Island include Castle Clinton National Monument; Federal Hall National Memorial; Theodore Roosevelt Birthplace National Historic Site; General Grant National Memorial; African Burial Ground National Monument; and Hamilton Grange National Memorial. Hundreds of private properties are listed on the National Register of Historic Places or as a National Historic Landmark, such as the Stonewall Inn in Greenwich Village, recognized as the catalyst of the modern gay rights movement.

After the agreement, Creative announced plans to produce accessories for the iPod by joining the Made for iPod program, which enables third-party vendors to offer iPod-compatible products.

Nicolas Chopin, Frédéric’s father, came from Lorraine, France, and moved to Poland in 1787 at the age of sixteen. He worked as a tutor for children of the Polish nobility and, in 1806, married a financially disadvantaged relative of the Skarbek family, one of his employers. Frédéric was baptized on Easter Sunday, April 23, 1810, in Brochów, the same church where his parents’ wedding had taken place. His godfather, after whom he was named, was Fryderyk Skarbek, then eighteen years old and a student of Nicolas Chopin. Frédéric was the second child and only son in the family, with an older sister named Ludwika (1807–1855), and two younger sisters, Izabela (1811–1881) and Emilia (1812–1827). Deeply attached to his adopted country, Nicolas insisted that Polish be spoken at home.

When he was 10 years old, West moved with his mother to China, where she was involved in an academic exchange program at a university in Nanjing. According to his mother, West was the only foreigner in his class, but he adjusted well and learned the language quickly, though he later forgot most of it. When asked about his high school grades, West said, "I got A's and B's. And I'm not even frontin'."

Go Set a Watchman, an earlier version of To Kill a Mockingbird, was released to the public amid controversy on July 14, 2015. This manuscript, which was finished in 1957, is set well after the events of To Kill a Mockingbird, though it does not serve as a direct sequel. The narrative centers on an adult Jean Louise “Scout” Finch, who returns from New York to visit her father, Atticus Finch, in Maycomb, Alabama, where she confronts the prejudice present in her hometown. The manuscript for Watchman was thought to be lost until it was reportedly found by Harper Lee’s attorney, Tonja Carter, a claim that has been the subject of much debate. Watchman features early incarnations of several characters later seen in To Kill a Mockingbird. Lee’s agent, Andrew Nurnberg, stated that Mockingbird was initially meant to be the first in a trilogy, with Watchman as the final installment and a shorter novel to connect them; however, this idea has been challenged by rare books specialist James S. Jaffe. After examining the manuscript for Lee’s lawyer, Jaffe determined that Watchman is simply another draft of To Kill a Mockingbird. Similarly, Jonathan Mahler described Watchman as merely the initial draft of Mockingbird, and the significant overlap between the texts, sometimes even identical passages, further undermines the trilogy claim.

In 1827, following the passing of Frédéric Chopin’s youngest sister, Emilia, the Chopin family relocated from their residence in the Warsaw University building next to Kazimierz Palace. They moved to new accommodations directly across the street, settling in the southern annex of the Krasiński Palace on Krakowskie Przedmieście. Chopin remained there until his departure from Warsaw in 1830. During this period, his parents continued to operate their boarding house, which accommodated male students. In the 20th century, the Chopin Family Parlour (Salonik Chopinów) was transformed into a museum. In 1829, a series of portraits featuring members of the Chopin family, including the earliest known likeness of Frédéric himself, was created by an artist.

Upon its release, the novel received a wide range of responses. Despite its immense sales and frequent inclusion in educational curricula, there is relatively little literary criticism of the work. Mary McDonough Murphy, an author who compiled reflections on To Kill a Mockingbird from various writers and notable individuals, described the novel as "an astonishing phenomenon." In 2006, librarians in the United Kingdom ranked To Kill a Mockingbird above the Bible as the book that every adult should read before dying. The story was brought to the big screen in 1962, with Robert Mulligan directing the adaptation and Horton Foote writing the screenplay, earning the film an Academy Award. Beginning in 1990, Harper Lee’s hometown of Monroeville, Alabama, has hosted an annual stage production based on the novel.

The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess (Japanese: ゼルダの伝説 トワイライトプリンセス, Hepburn: Zeruda no Densetsu: Towairaito Purinsesu) is an action-adventure game developed and published by Nintendo for the GameCube and Wii consoles. As the thirteenth installment in the Legend of Zelda series, it was originally planned for a GameCube release in November 2005. The launch was delayed by Nintendo to improve gameplay, add new features, and prepare a version for the Wii. The Wii edition was released in 2006, alongside the debut of the console.

New York City experiences a humid climate, with January being the coldest month. The city averages 234 days each year with at least some sunshine, and about 57% of possible sunshine annually. New York City falls under USDA 7b Plant Hardiness zone. The areas just north and west of the city are in a transition zone between different climate types.

The New York City Fire Department (FDNY) provides fire protection, technical rescue, response to various hazards, and emergency medical services throughout the five boroughs of New York City. It is the largest municipal fire department in the United States and the second largest in the world, after the Tokyo Fire Department. The FDNY employs approximately 11,080 uniformed firefighters and over 3,300 uniformed EMTs and paramedics. The department is often referred to as New York's Bravest.

In the 1970s, job losses due to industrial restructuring caused New York City to suffer from economic problems and rising crime rates. While a resurgence in the financial industry greatly improved the city's economic health in the 1980s, New York's crime rate continued to increase through that decade and into the beginning of the 1990s. By the mid 1990s, crime rates started to drop dramatically due to revised police strategies, improving economic opportunities, gentrification, and new residents, both American transplants and new immigrants from Asia and Latin America. Important new sectors, such as Silicon Alley, emerged in the city's economy. New York's population reached all-time highs in the 2000 Census and then again in the 2010 Census.
There are seven state parks within New York City. One of them, Riverbank State Park, is a 28-acre (110,000 m2) facility that rises 69 feet (21 m) over the Hudson River.

Truman Capote, a childhood friend of Harper Lee and a renowned author himself, contributed a statement for the first edition’s dust jacket, praising the novel as the work of “someone rare” with an exceptional sense of humor and a vivid outlook on life. Some have interpreted Capote’s remarks as implying that he either authored or significantly edited the book. In 2003, a newspaper in Tuscaloosa reported that Capote’s father claimed his son had written “almost all” of the novel. However, in 2006, a letter from Capote—donated to Monroeville’s literary heritage museum—revealed that in 1959 he told a Monroeville neighbor that Lee was in the process of writing a book soon to be published. Additionally, extensive correspondence between Lee and her editor provides strong evidence against the speculation that Capote was the true author. Harper Lee’s older sister also addressed these rumors, dismissing them as “the biggest lie ever told.”

As of 2013, the global advertising agencies Omnicom Group and Interpublic Group, both headquartered in Manhattan, had combined annual revenues of approximately US$21 billion, highlighting New York City's status as the top global center for the advertising industry, which is popularly known as "Madison Avenue." The city's fashion industry generates about $11 billion in annual wages for its workforce.

Starting with the fifth-generation iPod, Apple introduced a feature that allows users to set a maximum volume. In European Union countries, the sixth-generation iPod limits the top volume output to 100 decibels. Previously, Apple had to recall iPods from the French market because their volume exceeded the legally permitted threshold. Reports from late 2013 show that buyers of new sixth-generation iPods found a new setting that lets them turn off the EU volume restriction, made possible by updated software included with these newer devices. Earlier sixth-generation iPods cannot install this software update and therefore remain subject to the original volume limitation.

The city is known as the birthplace of various cultural movements, such as the Harlem Renaissance in literature and visual art, and abstract expressionism—also referred to as the New York School—in painting. It has played a significant role in the development of multiple music genres. The city is often celebrated in popular culture and is a frequent setting for books, movies, and television programs. One of the world's most prominent fashion events, New York Fashion Week, takes place here and receives extensive media coverage. The city has also been ranked as the top fashion capital of the world by the Global Language Monitor.

Manhattan Island is linked to New York City's outer boroughs and New Jersey by several tunnels as well. The Lincoln Tunnel, which carries 120,000 vehicles a day under the Hudson River between New Jersey and Midtown Manhattan, is the busiest vehicular tunnel in the world. The tunnel was built instead of a bridge to allow unfettered passage of large passenger and cargo ships that sailed through New York Harbor and up the Hudson River to Manhattan's piers. The Holland Tunnel, connecting Lower Manhattan to Jersey City, New Jersey, was the world's first mechanically ventilated vehicular tunnel when it opened in 1927. The Queens-Midtown Tunnel, built to relieve congestion on the bridges connecting Manhattan with Queens and Brooklyn, was the largest non-federal project in its time when it was completed in 1940. President Franklin D. Roosevelt was the first person to drive through it. The Hugh L. Carey Tunnel runs underneath Battery Park and connects the Financial District at the southern tip of Manhattan to Red Hook in Brooklyn.

In the fourth fiscal quarter of 2008, Apple disclosed that iPod sales contributed just 14.21% to the company’s total revenue. During a keynote event in September 2009, it was revealed that more than 220 million iPods had been sold cumulatively by that point. The steady drop in iPod purchases, which began in 2009, was anticipated by Apple’s Chief Financial Officer at the time, Peter Oppenheimer, who stated in June 2009: “We expect our traditional MP3 players to decline over time as we cannibalize ourselves with the iPod Touch and the iPhone.” From 2009 onward, iPod sales consistently fell each financial quarter, and notably, 2013 marked the first year since the iPod’s launch that no new model was released.

New York City is home to two NBA franchises: the Brooklyn Nets and the New York Knicks. The city’s representative in the Women’s National Basketball Association is the New York Liberty. The earliest national collegiate basketball championship was first hosted in New York in 1938 and continues to be held there. Basketball is deeply ingrained in the city’s culture, with games taking place in almost every park and many local youths advancing to prominent college teams and the NBA.

iPods have been criticized for alleged short life-span and fragile hard drives. A 2005 survey conducted on the MacInTouch website found that the iPod line had an average failure rate of 13.7% (although they note that comments from respondents indicate that "the true iPod failure rate may be lower than it appears"). It concluded that some models were more durable than others. In particular, failure rates for iPods employing hard drives was usually above 20% while those with flash memory had a failure rate below 10%. In late 2005, many users complained that the surface of the first generation iPod Nano can become scratched easily, rendering the screen unusable. A class action lawsuit was also filed. Apple initially considered the issue a minor defect, but later began shipping these iPods with protective sleeves.[citation needed]

While West had encountered controversy a year prior when he stormed out of the American Music Awards of 2004 after losing Best New Artist, the rapper's first large-scale controversy came just days following Late Registration's release, during a benefit concert for Hurricane Katrina victims. In September 2005, NBC broadcast A Concert for Hurricane Relief, and West was a featured speaker. When West was presenting alongside actor Mike Myers, he deviated from the prepared script. Myers spoke next and continued to read the script. Once it was West's turn to speak again, he said, "George Bush doesn't care about black people." West's comment reached much of the United States, leading to mixed reactions; President Bush would later call it one of the most "disgusting moments" of his presidency. West raised further controversy in January 2006 when he posed on the cover of Rolling Stone wearing a crown of thorns.

In 1785, the assembly of the Congress of the Confederation made New York the national capital shortly after the war. New York served as the last capital of the U.S. under the Articles of Confederation and became the first capital under the Constitution of the United States. In 1789, the first United States Congress and the Supreme Court of the United States each assembled for the first time, and the United States Bill of Rights was drafted, all at Federal Hall. By 1790, New York had become the largest city in the United States.

At the end of the Second Anglo-Dutch War, the English gained New Amsterdam (New York) in North America in exchange for Dutch control of an Indonesian island. Several intertribal wars among the Native Americans and some epidemics brought on by contact with the Europeans caused sizable population losses for the Lenape between the years 1660 and 1670. By 1700, the Lenape population had diminished to 200.

A rescue team indicated that only 2,300 people survived in Yingxiu, a town situated in Wenchuan County, which previously had several thousand residents. In Beichuan County, Sichuan Province, a significant number of individuals lost their lives, and many others sustained injuries; in addition, 80% of the buildings there were destroyed. The former county seat of Beichuan was left uninhabited and is now maintained as part of the Beichuan Earthquake Museum. In Dujiangyan, eight schools collapsed. During a rescue operation on the Lingyanshan Ropeway in Dujiangyan, a 56-year-old individual died; this incident occurred after 11 tourists from Taiwan had been trapped in cable cars since May 13 due to the earthquake. In Mianzhu City, a 4-year-old boy named Zhu Shaowei (traditional Chinese: 朱紹維; simplified Chinese: 朱绍维; pinyin: Zhū Shàowéi) was killed when a house fell on him, and another person was reported missing.

The GameCube edition of Twilight Princess earned three IGN awards: Best Artistic Design, Best Original Score, and Best Use of Sound. Both IGN and Nintendo Power honored the game with accolades for Best Graphics and Best Story. Twilight Princess was named Game of the Year by several outlets, including GameTrailers, 1UP.com, Electronic Gaming Monthly, Game Informer, Games Radar, GameSpy, Spacey Awards, X-Play, and Nintendo Power. Additionally, it won Best Adventure Game from the Game Critics Awards, X-Play, IGN, GameTrailers, 1UP.com, and Nintendo Power. The Game Critics Awards and GameSpy also recognized Twilight Princess as the Best Console Game. In Official Nintendo Magazine’s ranking of the 100 Greatest Nintendo Games of All Time, the game secured the 16th spot. IGN listed Twilight Princess as the fourth-best Wii title, while Nintendo Power placed it third among all Nintendo games released in the 2000s.

Starting in mid-2007, United, Continental, Delta, and Emirates became the first four major airlines to sign agreements to equip their aircraft with iPod seat connections. This complimentary service enables travelers to charge and power their iPods, as well as access their music and video collections directly through the personal seat-back screens. Initially, KLM and Air France were mentioned as potential partners in Apple’s initiative, but both airlines subsequently clarified that they were only considering the addition of these features and had not committed to the 2007 agreement.

While West had encountered controversy a year prior when he stormed out of the American Music Awards of 2004 after losing in a category for new artists, the rapper's first large-scale controversy came just days following Late Registration's release, during a benefit concert for Hurricane Katrina victims. In September 2005, NBC broadcast A Concert for Hurricane Relief, and West was a featured speaker. When West was presenting alongside actor Mike Myers, he deviated from the prepared script. Myers spoke next and continued to read the script. Once it was West's turn to speak again, he made a controversial statement about President Bush. West's comment reached much of the United States, leading to mixed reactions; President Bush would later call it one of the most "disgusting moments" of his presidency. West raised further controversy in January 2006 when he posed on the cover of Rolling Stone wearing a crown of thorns.

The Hudson River runs through the Hudson Valley and empties into New York Bay. From New York City up to Troy, New York, it functions as an estuary. This river forms a boundary along the edge of New York City. The East River, a tidal strait, connects Long Island Sound to the Upper New York Bay and divides the Bronx and Manhattan from Long Island. Separating most of Manhattan from the Bronx is the Harlem River, another tidal strait that links the Hudson and East Rivers. There is also a river that passes through both the Bronx and Westchester County.

Go Set a Watchman, an earlier version of To Kill a Mockingbird, was released to the public amid controversy on July 14, 2015. This manuscript, which was finished in 1957, takes place two decades after the events of To Kill a Mockingbird, though it does not serve as a direct sequel. The narrative centers on an adult Jean Louise “Scout” Finch, who returns from New York to visit her father, Atticus Finch, in Maycomb, Alabama, where she confronts the prejudice present in her hometown. The manuscript for Watchman was thought to be lost until it was reportedly found by Harper Lee’s attorney, Tonja Carter, a claim that has been the subject of much debate. Watchman features early incarnations of several characters later seen in To Kill a Mockingbird. Lee’s agent, Andrew Nurnberg, stated that Mockingbird was initially meant to be the first in a trilogy, with Watchman as the final installment and a shorter novel to connect them; however, this idea has been challenged by rare books specialist James S. Jaffe. After examining the manuscript for Lee’s lawyer, Jaffe determined that Watchman is simply another draft of To Kill a Mockingbird. Similarly, Jonathan Mahler described Watchman as merely the initial draft of Mockingbird, and the significant overlap between the texts, sometimes even identical passages, further undermines the trilogy claim.

Lee's childhood friend, author Truman Capote, wrote on the dust jacket of the first edition that the novel was the work of a rare and talented writer, praising its humor and likability. This comment has led some to speculate that Capote was involved in writing or editing the book. In 2003, a Tuscaloosa newspaper quoted Capote's biological father, Archulus Persons, as claiming that Capote had written "almost all" of the book. In 2006, a Capote letter was donated to Monroeville's literary heritage museum; in a letter to a neighbor in Monroeville in 1959, Capote mentioned that Lee was writing a book that would be published soon. Extensive notes between Lee and her editor also refute the rumor of Capote's authorship. Lee's older sister, Alice, responded to the rumor, calling it "the biggest lie ever told."

Filming in London included a brief shoot at City Hall in April 2015. In May, scenes were filmed on the Thames, featuring stunt work with a speedboat and a low-flying helicopter near Westminster Bridge. These sequences led to the temporary closure of both Westminster and Lambeth Bridges. Additional scenes were shot on the river near notable landmarks. The crew returned to the Thames less than a week later to film more scenes set on Westminster Bridge. The London Fire Brigade assisted on set by simulating rain and monitoring smoke effects. Cast members including Craig, Seydoux, Waltz, Harris, and Fiennes were seen during filming. Other scenes were filmed at various locations around London, such as Trafalgar Square. In early June, the crew and cast returned to the Thames to continue filming scenes previously started on the river.

After a buffer overflow flaw was identified in the Wii edition of Twilight Princess, hackers created an exploit called the "Twilight Hack." This allowed users to run custom code stored on a Secure Digital (SD) card by using a specially crafted save file, which triggered the game to execute unsigned code. This code could include various applications and homebrew software for the Wii. The Wii Menu versions 3.3 and 3.4 blocked the transfer of these exploited save files to the console, though workarounds were eventually found. The vulnerability was fully patched in Wii Menu version 4.0.

With the death of Zhengde and the rise of his successor, the politics at court shifted in favor of the Neo-Confucian establishment, which not only rejected the Portuguese embassy of Fernão Pires de Andrade, but also had a predisposed animosity towards Tibetan Buddhism and lamas. Evelyn S. Rawski, a professor in the Department of History at the University of Pittsburgh, writes that the Ming's unique relationship with Tibetan prelates essentially ended during this successor's reign, while Ming influence in certain regions was supplanted by other powers.

On May 16, China announced that it had received a total of $457 million in donations of cash and supplies to support rescue operations. Of this amount, $83 million came from various countries and four international organizations. Saudi Arabia emerged as the top donor, contributing nearly €40 million in financial aid along with relief materials valued at an extra €8 million.

Several independent stereo manufacturers have developed iPod-specific integration solutions. Alternative connection methods include adapter kits, audio input jacks, and FM transmitters such as the iTrip—although personal FM transmitters are illegal in some countries. Many car manufacturers have added audio input jacks as standard.

From a young age, West showed a strong interest in the arts, beginning to write poetry at just five years old. His mother remembered noticing his enthusiasm for drawing and music when he was in third grade. As he grew up in the city, West became heavily involved in the local hip hop community. He started rapping while in third grade and began creating his own music by seventh grade, eventually selling his compositions to other musicians. At thirteen, West wrote a rap song and convinced his mother to pay $25 per hour for studio time in a modest basement studio, where the microphone was suspended from the ceiling with a wire hanger. Although this was not her preference, his mother still supported his ambitions. Early in his career, West met producer and DJ No I.D., who soon became his mentor. No I.D. taught West how to sample and program beats after West received his first sampler at the age of fifteen.

In 1785, the assembly of the Congress of the Confederation made New York the national capital shortly after the war. New York served as the last capital of the U.S. under the Articles of Confederation and became the first capital under the Constitution of the United States. In 1789, the first United States Congress and the Supreme Court of the United States each assembled for the first time, and the United States Bill of Rights was drafted, all at Federal Hall. By 1790, New York had become the largest city in the United States.

According to the Köppen climate classification system, New York City is characterized by a humid subtropical climate (Cfa) when applying the 0 °C (32 °F) isotherm for its coldest month, which is January. The city is the northernmost major city in North America with this classification. The surrounding suburbs are located in a transitional climate area. On average, New York experiences sunshine on more than half of the days each year, receiving about 57% of the possible sunlight annually. The city is designated as USDA Plant Hardiness Zone 7b.

The dock connector enabled the iPod to interface with various accessories that enhance its ability to play music, videos, and photos. While Apple produced a limited number of accessories—including the iPod Hi-Fi, which is no longer available—most accessories are created by third-party companies like Belkin and Griffin. Certain peripherals operate through their own interface, whereas others utilize the iPod’s display. Since the dock connector is a proprietary technology, third-party manufacturers must pay royalties to Apple in order to use it.

Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts, anchoring Lincoln Square on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, is a major cultural hub. The Lee Strasberg Theatre and Film Institute is located in Union Square, and Tisch School of the Arts is based at New York University. Central Park SummerStage presents performances of free plays and music in Central Park.

New York—often referred to as New York City or the City of New York to distinguish it from the State of New York, of which it is a part—is the most populous city in the United States and the center of the New York metropolitan area, one of the largest urban agglomerations in the world. A global power city, New York exerts a significant impact upon commerce, finance, media, art, fashion, research, technology, education, and entertainment, its fast pace defining the term New York minute. Home to the headquarters of the United Nations, New York is an important center for international diplomacy and has been described as the cultural and financial capital of the world.

In December, Beyoncé, along with various other celebrities, participated in a video campaign for "Demand A Plan," a bipartisan initiative by a group of 950 US mayors and others designed to influence the federal government to reconsider its gun control laws. Beyoncé became an ambassador for the 2012 World Humanitarian Day campaign, donating her song "I Was Here" and its music video, filmed at the UN, to support the cause. In 2013, it was announced that Beyoncé would collaborate with Salma Hayek and Frida Giannini on Gucci's "Chime for Change" campaign, which aims to promote female empowerment. The campaign, which aired on February 28, featured her new music. A concert for the cause took place on June 1, 2013, in London and included other acts such as Ellie Goulding, Florence and the Machine, and Rita Ora. Ahead of the concert, she appeared in a campaign video released on May 15, 2013, where she, along with Cameron Diaz, John Legend, and Kylie Minogue, spoke about inspiration from their mothers, while other artists celebrated inspiration from women in their lives. Viewers were invited to submit photos of women who inspired them, with a selection shown at the concert. Beyoncé said about her mother, Tina Knowles, that her gift was "finding the best qualities in every human being." During the concert, attendees could choose between several projects supporting education for women and girls. Beyoncé is also involved in "Miss a Meal," a food-donation campaign, and supports Goodwill charity through online auctions at Charitybuzz that help create jobs in Europe and the U.S.

New York City covers a total area of 468.9 square miles (1,214 km²). A portion of this area consists of water, totaling 164.1 square miles (425 km²). The city's highest elevation reaches 409.8 feet (124.9 meters) above sea level and is located within a largely forested summit area that forms part of the Staten Island Greenbelt.

The Hudson River passes through the Hudson Valley and continues past New York City. Between New York City and Troy, the river is considered an estuary. The Hudson River forms a boundary along one side of the city. The East River—a tidal strait—connects to Long Island Sound and separates the Bronx and Manhattan from Long Island. The Harlem River, another tidal strait located between the East and Hudson Rivers, separates most of Manhattan from the Bronx. The Bronx River, which flows through the Bronx and Westchester County, is the only river in the city that is entirely fresh water.

iPods have faced criticism for their reportedly limited lifespan and the susceptibility of some internal components to failure. In 2005, a technology-focused website conducted a survey to find out how frequently iPods stopped working. The results indicated an average failure rate of 13.7% across different iPod models, though participant feedback suggested the real rate might be somewhat lower. The survey also found that some models were more durable than others; iPods with hard drive storage generally had failure rates above 20%, while those using flash memory had rates below 10%. Later in 2005, many owners of a particular iPod model raised concerns about the device’s surface being easily scratched, which sometimes made the display difficult to read. This issue led to a class action lawsuit. Although the company initially described the problem as minor, it eventually began providing protective sleeves with these iPods to address customer concerns.
