New York has also frequently been ranked the top fashion capital of the world on the annual list compiled by the Global Language Monitor.

According to Chen, Yonten Gyatso, the fourth Dalai Lama, received the title "Master of Vajradhara" along with an official seal from the Wanli Emperor in 1616. The Biography of the Fourth Dalai Lama records that Soinam Lozui was responsible for delivering the Emperor’s seal to Yonten Gyatso. In that same year, the Wanli Emperor extended an invitation to Yonten Gyatso to visit Beijing. However, similar to the previous Dalai Lama, Yonten Gyatso passed away before he could undertake the trip.

On September 17, 2011, demonstrations known as Occupy Wall Street started in Zuccotti Park, located in the Financial District of Lower Manhattan. These protests attracted international attention and led to the emergence of the Occupy movement, which challenged social and economic inequality around the globe.

Major tourist destinations include Times Square; Broadway theater productions; the Empire State Building; the Statue of Liberty; Ellis Island; the United Nations Headquarters; museums such as the Metropolitan Museum of Art; greenspaces such as Central Park and Washington Square Park; Rockefeller Center; a Chinatown in Manhattan; luxury shopping along notable avenues; and events such as the Halloween Parade in Greenwich Village; the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade; the lighting of a famous Christmas tree at Rockefeller Center; the St. Patrick's Day parade; seasonal activities such as ice skating in Central Park in the wintertime; the Tribeca Film Festival; and free performances in Central Park at Summerstage. Major attractions in the boroughs outside Manhattan include Flushing Meadows-Corona Park and the Unisphere in Queens; the Bronx Zoo; Coney Island in Brooklyn; and the New York Botanical Garden in the Bronx. A large ferris wheel was under construction at the northern shore of Staten Island in 2015, overlooking notable city landmarks.

New York City is known for its dynamic food culture, influenced by a wide range of communities. Foods such as bagels, cheesecake, and pizza have become staples, and today, a variety of eateries—including sandwich shops, diners, and coffeehouses—can be found across the city. There are about 4,000 mobile food vendors, many operated by immigrants, offering a range of international dishes as part of the city’s street food. According to Michelin, the city is home to nearly one thousand highly regarded fine dining establishments. The New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene oversees the inspection of the city’s 24,000 restaurants and assigns letter grades based on their evaluations.

The novel To Kill a Mockingbird was first published in 1960. It quickly achieved critical acclaim, earning the Pulitzer Prize and establishing itself as a cornerstone of contemporary American literature. The author drew inspiration for the story’s plot and characters from personal experiences, particularly from people in their family and neighborhood, and from a real-life incident that took place close to their hometown in 1936, when they were ten.

Go Set a Watchman, an earlier version of To Kill a Mockingbird, generated controversy upon its release. This manuscript, completed prior to Mockingbird, is set two decades after the events of that novel, though it does not function as a direct sequel. The story follows an adult Jean Louise “Scout” Finch, who returns from New York to visit her father, Atticus Finch, in Maycomb, Alabama, where she confronts the prejudice present in her hometown. The manuscript for Watchman was thought to be lost until it was reportedly found by Harper Lee’s attorney, Tonja Carter, a claim that has been the subject of much debate. Watchman features early incarnations of several characters later seen in To Kill a Mockingbird. Lee’s agent, Andrew Nurnberg, stated that Mockingbird was initially meant to be the first in a trilogy, with Watchman as the final installment and a shorter novel to connect them; however, this idea has been challenged by rare books specialist James S. Jaffe. After examining the manuscript for Lee’s lawyer, Jaffe determined that Watchman is simply another draft of To Kill a Mockingbird. Similarly, Jonathan Mahler described Watchman as merely the initial draft of Mockingbird, and the significant overlap between the texts, sometimes even identical passages, further undermines the trilogy claim.

Thomas Newman returned as Spectre's composer. Rather than composing the score once the film had moved into post-production, Newman worked during filming. The theatrical trailer released in July 2015 contained a rendition of John Barry's On Her Majesty's Secret Service theme. Mendes revealed that the final film would have more than one hundred minutes of music. The soundtrack album was released on 23 October 2015 in the UK and 6 November 2015 in the USA on the Decca Records label.

The Staten Island Ferry is the world's busiest ferry route, carrying approximately 20 million passengers annually along its 5.2-mile (8.4 km) route and operating 24 hours a day. The ferry connects Staten Island with another borough of New York City. Other ferry systems also transport commuters between Manhattan and various locations within the city and the surrounding metropolitan area.

On September 17, 2011, demonstrations known as Occupy Wall Street started in Zuccotti Park, located in the Financial District of Lower Manhattan. These protests attracted international attention and led to the emergence of the Occupy movement, which challenged social and economic inequality around the globe.

iPods have been criticized for their allegedly short life-span and fragile hard drives. A 2005 survey conducted on the MacInTouch website found that the iPod line had an average failure rate of 13.7%, though they noted that comments from respondents suggested the actual failure rate might be lower. The survey concluded that some models were more durable than others. In particular, iPods with hard drives tended to have failure rates above 20%, while those using flash memory had rates below 10%. In late 2005, many users complained that the surface of the first generation iPod Nano could become scratched easily, making the screen unusable. A class action lawsuit was also filed. Apple initially considered the issue a minor defect.[citation needed]

The dock connector allowed the iPod to connect with a range of accessories that expand its capabilities for playing music, videos, and photos. While Apple offered a small selection of its own accessories—one of which is no longer available—most accessories are made by third-party companies such as Belkin and Griffin. Some peripherals use their own interface, while others interact with the iPod’s display. Because the dock connector is proprietary, third-party manufacturers are required to pay royalties to Apple to use it.

The National Hockey League teams based in New York City are the New York Rangers and the New York Islanders. Additionally, the New Jersey Devils are located in the metropolitan area and play their home games in Newark, New Jersey.

After graduating from high school, West received a scholarship to attend Chicago's American Academy of Art in 1997 and began taking painting classes, but shortly after transferred to Chicago State University to study English. He soon realized that his busy class schedule was detrimental to his musical work, and eventually decided to leave college to pursue his musical dreams. This action greatly displeased his mother, who was also a professor at the university. She later commented, "It was drummed into my head that college is the ticket to a good life... but some career goals don't require college. For Kanye to make an album called College Dropout it was more about having the guts to embrace who you are, rather than following the path society has carved out for you."

Yonten Gyatso, the fourth Dalai Lama, was granted the title "Master of Vajradhara" by the Wanli Emperor in 1616. That same year, the Emperor invited Yonten Gyatso to visit Beijing. However, Yonten Gyatso, like his predecessor, passed away before he could make the journey.

Beyoncé's fan base is widely known as the Bey Hive. This term became popular after fans promoted it through social media platforms and online news coverage during various competitions. Previously, Beyoncé's fans were known by a different name, which combined her name with another word. The current name, Bey Hive, is the most recent and recognized term for her supporters.

During the years immediately following the novel's publication, Harper Lee enjoyed the attention its popularity brought her, granting interviews, visiting schools, and attending events honoring the book. In 1961, To Kill a Mockingbird was awarded the Pulitzer Prize, which stunned Lee. That same year, it also received the Brotherhood Award of the National Conference of Christians and Jews, and in 1962, it was named Paperback of the Year by Bestsellers magazine. Beginning in 1964, Lee started to turn down interviews, expressing frustration with repetitive questions and growing uneasy with the level of attention she received. From that point on, she declined to speak with reporters about the book. She also consistently refused to write an introduction, stating in 1995 that introductions diminish the pleasure and anticipation of reading, and that Mockingbird has endured without one.

In 2013, Omnicom Group and Interpublic Group, two of the world’s largest advertising agencies headquartered in Manhattan, together generated about US$21 billion in annual revenue. This underscores New York City’s status as the leading global hub for the advertising sector, commonly known as "Madison Avenue." The fashion industry in New York City pays out roughly $11 billion in wages each year and is a major employer in the city.

The Bey Hive is the name given to Beyoncé's fan base. Fans were previously titled "The Beyontourage", (a portmanteau of Beyoncé and entourage). The name Bey Hive derives from the word beehive, purposely misspelled to resemble her first name, and was penned by fans after petitions on the online social networking service Twitter and online news reports during competitions.

In soccer, New York City is represented by New York City FC of Major League Soccer, who play their home games at Yankee Stadium. The New York Red Bulls play their home games at Red Bull Arena in nearby Harrison, New Jersey. Historically, the city is known for the New York Cosmos, the highly successful former professional soccer team which was the American home of Pelé, one of the world's most famous soccer players. A new version of the New York Cosmos was formed in 2010, and began play in the second division North American Soccer League in 2013. The Cosmos play their home games at James M. Shuart Stadium on the campus of Hofstra University, just outside the New York City limits in Hempstead, New York.

The annual United States Open Tennis Championships is one of the world's four Grand Slam tennis tournaments and is held at the National Tennis Center in Flushing Meadows-Corona Park, Queens. The New York Marathon is one of the world's largest, and the 2004–2006 events hold the top three places in the marathons with the largest number of finishers, including 37,866 finishers in 2006. The Millrose Games is an annual track and field meet whose featured event is the Wanamaker Mile. Boxing is also a prominent part of the city's sporting scene, with events like the Amateur Boxing Golden Gloves being held at Madison Square Garden each year. The city is also considered the host of the Belmont Stakes, the last, longest and oldest of horse racing's Triple Crown races, held just over the city's border at Belmont Park on the first or second Sunday of June. The city also hosted the 1932 U.S. Open golf tournament and the 1930 and 1939 PGA Championships, and has been host city for both events several times, most notably for nearby Winged Foot Golf Club.

When he was 10 years old, Kanye West and his mother relocated to Nanjing, China, because she was participating in a teaching exchange at a university there. During their time there, West was the sole foreign student in his class, but he adapted easily and learned the language rapidly, though he later lost much of his fluency. Reflecting on his high school performance, West stated, "I got A's and B's. And I'm not even frontin'."

In the period following the release of her novel, Harper Lee embraced the recognition it brought, participating in interviews, visiting educational institutions, and attending ceremonies dedicated to the book. To Kill a Mockingbird received the Pulitzer Prize while it was still holding a spot on the bestseller list for its 41st consecutive week, a development that took Lee by surprise. That same period, the novel was also honored with the Brotherhood Award from the National Conference of Christians and Jews. The following year, Bestsellers magazine named it Paperback of the Year. Beginning in 1964, Lee started refusing interview requests, expressing frustration with repetitive questions and growing uneasy with the level of attention, which she felt resembled celebrity publicity. From that point onward, she consistently declined to speak to journalists about her book. Lee also refused to write an introduction for the novel, stating in 1995 that such prefaces diminish enjoyment, spoil anticipation, and hinder curiosity, and that To Kill a Mockingbird had endured over time without the need for one.

In 1827, following the passing of Frédéric Chopin’s youngest sister, Emilia, the Chopin family relocated from their residence in the Warsaw University building next to Kazimierz Palace. They moved to new accommodations directly across the street, settling in the southern annex of the Krasiński Palace on Krakowskie Przedmieście. Chopin remained there until his departure from Warsaw in 1830. During this period, his parents continued to operate their boarding house, which accommodated male students. In the 20th century, the Chopin Family Parlour (Salonik Chopinów) was transformed into a museum. In 1829, Ambroży Mieroszewski, an artist, created a series of portraits featuring members of the Chopin family, including the earliest known likeness of Frédéric himself.

In 2013, Omnicom Group and Interpublic Group, two of the world’s largest advertising agencies headquartered in Manhattan, together generated about US$21 billion in annual revenue. This underscores New York City’s status as the leading global hub for the advertising sector, commonly known as "Madison Avenue." The fashion industry in New York City employs around 180,000 people and pays out roughly $11 billion in wages each year.
New York City is home to seven state parks. One of these, Riverbank State Park, covers 28 acres (110,000 m²) and is situated 69 feet (21 meters) above the Hudson River at its highest point.

The story centers on the main character, who strives to save Hyrule from being overtaken by a corrupted parallel dimension called the Twilight Realm. In this quest, the hero transforms between two forms and is aided by a mysterious creature named Midna. The events unfold centuries after earlier adventures and occur in a timeline separate from that of The Wind Waker.

While West had encountered controversy a year prior when he stormed out of the American Music Awards of 2004 after losing in a specific category, the rapper's first large-scale controversy came just days following Late Registration's release, during a benefit concert for Hurricane Katrina victims. In September 2005, NBC broadcast A Concert for Hurricane Relief, and West was a featured speaker. When West was presenting alongside actor Mike Myers, he deviated from the prepared script. Myers spoke next and continued to read the script. Once it was West's turn to speak again, he made a highly critical comment about President Bush. West's statement reached much of the United States, leading to mixed reactions; President Bush would later call it one of the most "disgusting moments" of his presidency. West raised further controversy in January 2006 when he appeared on the cover of a major magazine wearing a crown of thorns.

The New York City Fire Department (FDNY), provides fire protection, technical rescue, primary response to biological, chemical, and radioactive hazards, and emergency medical services for the five boroughs of New York City. The New York City Fire Department is the largest municipal fire department in the United States and the second largest in the world after the Tokyo Fire Department. The FDNY employs approximately 11,080 uniformed firefighters and over 3,300 uniformed EMTs and paramedics. The FDNY's motto is New York's Bravest.

New York City has played a major role in shaping various cultural movements, including the Harlem Renaissance and abstract expressionism, which is also known as the New York School. The city has influenced a wide range of music genres and is frequently featured in popular culture, serving as the setting for numerous books, films, and television series. One of the most significant fashion events held there is New York Fashion Week, which attracts considerable media coverage. The Global Language Monitor has repeatedly ranked New York as the leading fashion capital of the world in its annual reports.

The narrative centers around a hero who strives to save Hyrule from being consumed by a dark parallel world called the Twilight Realm. Throughout the journey, this hero transforms between a Hylian form and that of a wolf, receiving guidance and support from a mysterious being named Midna. This storyline unfolds several centuries after the events of Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and exists in a separate timeline from The Wind Waker.

Beginning in 1236, the Mongol prince Kublai received a substantial appanage in northern China from his overlord. Karma Pakshi, who was the second Karmapa Lama and the leader of the Karma Kagyu school of Tibetan Buddhism, declined Kublai’s invitation. As a result, Kublai turned to Drogön Chögyal Phagpa, the nephew and successor of Sakya Pandita, inviting him to his court in 1253. Kublai established a distinctive partnership with Phagpa, whereby Kublai was acknowledged as the supreme authority in political matters, while Phagpa served as his chief religious advisor. Furthermore, Kublai appointed Drogön Chögyal Phagpa as the head of the Bureau of Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs and as the priest-king of Tibet, which at that time consisted of thirteen states governed by myriarchies.

During this period, the Tumed Mongols began to settle in the Kokonor area, which is present-day Qinghai. Under the leadership of Altan Khan, they launched raids against the Ming Chinese frontier, reaching deep into the region. According to Klieger, Altan Khan’s activities in the west significantly diminished Ming influence and their connections with Tibet. In 1571, Altan Khan established peace with the Ming dynasty. Subsequently, he invited Sönam Gyatso, a prominent leader of the Gelug school, to meet him in Amdo (now Qinghai).

The remaining band members recorded "Independent Women Part I", which appeared on the soundtrack to the 2000 film, Charlie's Angels. It became their best-charting single, topping the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 chart for eleven consecutive weeks. While Destiny's Child was completing their third album, Beyoncé landed a major role in the MTV made-for-television film, Carmen: A Hip Hopera, starring alongside American actor Mekhi Phifer. Set in Philadelphia, the film is a modern interpretation of the 19th century opera Carmen by French composer Georges Bizet. When the third album Survivor was released, Luckett and Roberson filed a lawsuit claiming that the songs were aimed at them. The album debuted at number one on the U.S. Billboard 200, with first-week sales of 663,000 copies sold. The album spawned other number-one hits, "Bootylicious" and the title track, "Survivor", the latter of which earned the group a Grammy Award for Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals. After releasing their holiday album 8 Days of Christmas, the group later decided to focus on solo careers.

The GameCube edition of Twilight Princess earned three IGN awards: Best Artistic Design, Best Original Score, and Best Use of Sound. Both IGN and Nintendo Power honored the game with accolades for Best Graphics and Best Story. Twilight Princess was named Game of the Year by several outlets. Additionally, it won Best Adventure Game from multiple sources, and the Game Critics Awards and GameSpy recognized Twilight Princess as the Best Console Game. In Official Nintendo Magazine’s ranking of the 100 Greatest Nintendo Games of All Time, the game was included in the top 20. IGN listed Twilight Princess as the fourth-best Wii title, while Nintendo Power placed it third among all Nintendo games released in the 2000s.

The FDNY headquarters is located at 9 MetroTech Center in Downtown Brooklyn, and the FDNY Fire Academy is located on Randalls Island. There are three Bureau of Fire Communications alarm offices which receive and dispatch alarms to appropriate units. One office, at 11 Metrotech Center in Brooklyn, houses Manhattan/Citywide, Brooklyn, and Staten Island Fire Communications. The Bronx and Queens offices are in separate buildings.

Unlike other major American cities, New York is uniquely split between two primary US district courts, each with its own main courthouse located in a different borough. The Southern District of New York’s main courthouse is situated on Foley Square in Manhattan. The Eastern District of New York’s main courthouse is found in Brooklyn, with its jurisdiction including Staten Island. Additionally, New York is home to the US Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit and the US Court of International Trade, both of which are also located on Foley Square.

Several independent stereo brands, such as JVC, Pioneer, Kenwood, Alpine, Sony, and Harman Kardon, have developed integration solutions specifically for iPods. Other ways to connect an iPod include using adapter kits that utilize either the cassette deck or the CD changer port, audio input jacks, and FM transmitters like the iTrip. However, it should be noted that personal FM transmitters are prohibited in certain countries. Additionally, audio input jacks have become a standard feature offered by many automobile manufacturers.

The Occupy Wall Street protests began on September 17, 2011, in Zuccotti Park, located in the Financial District of Manhattan. The demonstrations drew widespread attention and inspired a broader movement focused on social and economic issues.

Manhattan Island is connected to surrounding areas by several tunnels. One of these, which accommodates 120,000 vehicles daily, was constructed instead of a bridge to allow large passenger and cargo ships to pass freely to Manhattan's piers. Another, the Holland Tunnel, links Lower Manhattan to Jersey City, New Jersey, and was the world's first mechanically ventilated vehicular tunnel when it opened in 1927. The Queens-Midtown Tunnel, completed in 1940 to help reduce congestion on existing bridges, was the largest non-federal project of its era. President Franklin D. Roosevelt was the first person to drive through this tunnel. Additionally, the Hugh L. Carey Tunnel runs underneath Battery Park and connects the Financial District at Manhattan’s southern tip to Red Hook in Brooklyn.

West demonstrated an affinity for the arts at an early age; he began writing poetry when he was five years old. His mother recalled that she first took notice of West's passion for drawing and music when he was in the third grade. Growing up in the city, West became deeply involved in its hip hop scene. He started rapping in the third grade and began making musical compositions in the seventh grade, eventually selling them to other artists. At age thirteen, West wrote a rap song and began to persuade his mother to pay $25 an hour for time in a recording studio. It was a small, crude basement studio where a microphone hung from the ceiling by a wire clothes hanger. Although this wasn't what West's mother wanted, she nonetheless supported him. West crossed paths with producer/DJ No I.D., with whom he quickly formed a close friendship. No I.D. soon became West's mentor, and it was from him that West learned how to sample and program beats after he received his first sampler at age 15.

Several independent stereo manufacturers have developed iPod-specific integration solutions. Alternative connection methods include adapter kits, audio input jacks, and FM transmitters such as the iTrip—although personal FM transmitters are illegal in some countries. Many car manufacturers have added audio input jacks as standard.

In 1827, soon after the death of Chopin's youngest sister Emilia, the family moved from the Warsaw University building, adjacent to the Kazimierz Palace, to lodgings just across the street from the university, in the south annex of the Krasiński Palace on Krakowskie Przedmieście,[n 5] where Chopin lived until he left Warsaw in 1830.[n 6] Here his parents continued running their boarding house for male students; the Chopin Family Parlour (Salonik Chopinów) became a museum in the 20th century. In 1829 the artist Ambroży Mieroszewski executed a set of portraits of Chopin family members, including the first known portrait of the composer.[n 7]

Using the 0 °C (32 °F) coldest month (January) isotherm, New York City itself experiences a humid subtropical climate and is thus the northernmost major city on the North American continent with this categorization. The suburbs to the immediate north and west lie in the transition zone from a humid subtropical to a humid continental climate. The area averages 234 days with at least some sunshine annually, and averages 57% of possible sunshine annually, accumulating 2,535 hours of sunshine per year.

After graduating from high school, Kanye West began his studies at an art school in Chicago in 1997, where he initially took painting courses. Not long after, he transferred to Chicago State University, focusing his studies on English. However, he soon found that balancing his academic workload with his passion for music was challenging. At the age of 20, Kanye made the decision to leave college in order to dedicate himself fully to his music career. This choice was met with disappointment from his mother, a professor at the same university. She later reflected, "I was always taught that college was the key to a successful life... but not every career requires a degree. For Kanye, creating the album College Dropout was more about having the courage to be true to himself than simply following the conventional route."

The GameCube edition of Twilight Princess earned three IGN awards: Best Artistic Design, Best Original Score, and Best Use of Sound. Both IGN and Nintendo Power honored the game with accolades for Best Graphics and Best Story. Twilight Princess was named Game of the Year by several outlets and won Best Adventure Game from multiple organizations, including the Game Critics Awards, X-Play, IGN, GameTrailers, 1UP.com, and Nintendo Power. The Game Critics Awards and GameSpy also recognized Twilight Princess as the Best Console Game. The game was featured in Official Nintendo Magazine’s ranking of the 100 Greatest Nintendo Games of All Time. IGN included Twilight Princess among the top Wii titles, and Nintendo Power recognized it as one of the best Nintendo games released in the 2000s.

Following the discovery of a buffer overflow vulnerability in the Wii version of Twilight Princess, an exploit known as the "Twilight Hack" was developed, allowing the execution of custom code from a Secure Digital (SD) card on the console. A properly designed save file would cause the game to load unsigned code, which could include Executable and Linkable Format (ELF) programs and homebrew Wii applications. Versions 3.3 and 3.4 of the Wii Menu prevented copying exploited save files onto the console until circumvention methods were discovered, and version 4.0 of the Wii Menu patched the vulnerability.

The Battle of Long Island, the largest battle of the American Revolutionary War, was fought in August 1776 entirely within the modern-day borough of Brooklyn. After the battle, in which the Americans were defeated, leaving subsequent smaller armed engagements following in its wake, the city became the British military and political base of operations in North America. The city was a haven for Loyalist refugees, as well as escaped slaves who joined the British lines for freedom newly promised by the Crown for all fighters. As many as 10,000 escaped slaves crowded into the city during the British occupation. When the British forces evacuated at the close of the war in 1783, they transported 3,000 freedmen for resettlement in Nova Scotia. They resettled other freedmen in England and the Caribbean.

Italian designer Roberto Cavalli has noted that Beyoncé incorporates a variety of fashion styles to complement her music during performances. Her mother collaborated on a book released in 2002 called Destiny's Style, which details the influence of fashion on the group's achievements. The B'Day Anthology Video Album includes numerous scenes focused on fashion, highlighting both traditional and modern clothing choices. In 2007, Beyoncé appeared on the cover of a major swimsuit magazine, making her the second African American woman to do so, following Tyra Banks. Additionally, she has been recognized for her sense of style by various publications.

Located in the borough of Manhattan, Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts serves as the focal point of Lincoln Square, which is on the Upper West Side. This well-known complex is home to several major cultural institutions. The Lee Strasberg Theatre and Film Institute is located in Union Square, and the Tisch School of the Arts is part of New York University. Additionally, Central Park SummerStage offers complimentary theater and musical performances within Central Park.

When he was 10, West moved with his mother to China, where she was teaching at a university as part of an exchange program. According to his mother, West was the only foreigner in his class, but settled in well and quickly picked up the language, although he has since forgotten most of it. When asked about his grades in high school, West replied, "I got A's and B's. And I'm not even frontin'."

New York City is home to the Brooklyn Nets, an NBA franchise. The city’s women’s basketball team is known as the New York Liberty. The National Invitation Tournament, the earliest national collegiate basketball championship, was first hosted in New York in 1938 and continues to be held there. Basketball is deeply ingrained in the city’s culture, with games taking place in almost every park and many local youths advancing to prominent college teams and the NBA.

During April and May 2015, filming sessions took place at various locations in London, including City Hall, the Thames, and areas near Westminster Bridge and Lambeth Bridge. Nighttime stunt sequences were shot on the river, featuring actors in a speedboat and a helicopter flying low near Westminster Bridge. For these scenes, certain bridges were temporarily inaccessible to the public. Additional filming occurred on the Thames close to the MI6 headquarters at Vauxhall Cross, as well as in Trafalgar Square. To create realistic weather effects, the London Fire Brigade assisted by providing simulated rain and overseeing the use of smoke during filming. Actors such as Craig, Seydoux, Waltz, Harris, and Fiennes were present during these shoots. Prior to the river scenes, sequences with Fiennes were filmed at a restaurant in Covent Garden. In early June, the production team, along with several cast members, returned to the Thames to continue work on previously started river scenes.

Chen states that the fourth Dalai Lama, Yonten Gyatso, was granted the title "Master of Vajradhara" by the Wanli Emperor in 1616. The Wanli Emperor had invited Yonten Gyatso to Beijing that year, but, as with his predecessor, he died before being able to make the journey.

Apple introduced a new version of the iPod Touch in July 2015, officially launching it on the Apple Store on July 15 of that year. This sixth-generation iPod Touch features several significant upgrades, including the advanced A8 processor and an improved display. Its processing core delivers performance more than five times faster than earlier models, making it comparable to the iPhone 5S. The latest iPod Touch is available in a variety of color options.

The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess (Japanese: ゼルダの伝説 トワイライトプリンセス, Hepburn: Zeruda no Densetsu: Towairaito Purinsesu) was developed and published by Nintendo for the GameCube and Wii consoles. As part of the Legend of Zelda franchise, the game’s release was delayed by Nintendo to improve the experience and to prepare a version for the Wii system. The Wii edition was released in North America in November 2006, coinciding with the launch of the console, and the GameCube version became available worldwide in December 2006.

Manhattan Island is linked to New York City's outer boroughs and New Jersey by several tunnels. The Lincoln Tunnel, which carries 120,000 vehicles a day under the Hudson River between New Jersey and Midtown Manhattan, is the busiest vehicular tunnel in the world. The tunnel was built instead of a bridge to allow unfettered passage of large passenger and cargo ships that sailed through New York Harbor and up the Hudson River to Manhattan's piers. The Holland Tunnel, connecting Lower Manhattan to Jersey City, New Jersey, was the world's first mechanically ventilated vehicular tunnel when it opened in 1927. The Queens-Midtown Tunnel, built to relieve congestion on the bridges connecting Manhattan with Queens and Brooklyn, was the largest non-federal project in its time when it was completed in 1940. The Hugh L. Carey Tunnel runs underneath Battery Park and connects the Financial District at the southern tip of Manhattan to Red Hook in Brooklyn.

New York is the most important source of political fundraising in the United States, as four of the top five ZIP codes in the nation for political contributions are located in Manhattan. The leading ZIP code, 10021, generated the most money for the 2004 presidential campaigns of both major candidates. The city has a strong imbalance of payments with the national and state governments. It receives 83 cents in services for every $1 it sends to the federal government in taxes, meaning it annually sends $11.4 billion more than it receives back. The city also sends an additional $11 billion more each year to the state government than it receives in return.

Beyoncé's fan base is known as the Bey Hive. This name is inspired by the word "beehive," intentionally altered to reflect her first name. Over time, the term Bey Hive became widely used to describe her supporters. Previously, fans were referred to by a different name.

The National Hockey League teams based in New York City are the New York Rangers and the New York Islanders. Additionally, the New Jersey Devils are located in the metropolitan area and play their home games in Newark, New Jersey.

The National Park Service oversees both the Statue of Liberty National Monument and the Ellis Island Immigration Museum, which are located in the states of New York and New Jersey. Beginning in 1236, the Mongol prince Kublai—who would later become Khagan and rule from 1260 to 1294—received a substantial appanage in northern China from his overlord, Ögedei Khan. As a result, Kublai turned to Drogön Chögyal Phagpa (1235–1280), the nephew and successor of Sakya Pandita, inviting him to his court in 1253. Kublai established a distinctive partnership with Phagpa, whereby Kublai was acknowledged as the supreme authority in political matters, while Phagpa served as his chief religious advisor. Furthermore, Kublai appointed Drogön Chögyal Phagpa as the head of the Bureau of Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs and as the priest-king of Tibet, which at that time consisted of thirteen states governed by myriarchies.

Kublai instituted a unique relationship with the Phagpa lama, which recognized Kublai as a superior sovereign in political affairs and the Phagpa lama as the senior instructor to Kublai in religious affairs. Kublai also made Drogön Chögyal Phagpa the director of the government agency known as the Bureau of Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs and the ruling priest-king of Tibet, which comprised thirteen different states ruled by myriarchies.

In the period following the release of her novel, Harper Lee embraced the recognition it brought, participating in interviews, visiting educational institutions, and attending ceremonies dedicated to the book. From that point onward, she consistently declined to speak to journalists about her book. Lee also refused to write an introduction for the novel, stating in 1995 that such prefaces diminish enjoyment, spoil anticipation, and hinder curiosity, and that To Kill a Mockingbird had endured over time without the need for one.

Nicolas Chopin, Frédéric’s father, was originally from Lorraine, France, and moved to Poland as a young man. Frédéric was baptized in Brochów, in the same church where his parents had wed. He was the second child and only son in the family, with an older sister named Ludwika (1807–1855), and two younger sisters, Izabela (1811–1881) and Emilia (1812–1827). During the late 20th century, New York City experienced significant economic and social changes. The city faced major economic challenges and a surge in crime as a result of widespread job losses linked to shifts in the industrial sector. Although the financial industry experienced a revival in the 1980s that significantly boosted the city's economy, crime rates continued to climb throughout that decade and into the early 1990s. It was not until the mid-1990s that crime began to decline sharply, a change attributed to updated policing methods, better economic prospects, gentrification, and an influx of new residents, including both domestic migrants and immigrants from Asia and Latin America. The 1990s also saw the rise of new economic sectors in New York, such as Silicon Alley. The city’s population reached record levels in the 2000 Census and set another new peak in the 2010 Census.

Though he had developed his rapping long before he began producing, it was often a challenge for West to be accepted as a rapper, and he struggled to attain a record deal. Multiple record companies ignored him because he did not fit the dominant image in mainstream hip hop at the time. After a series of meetings with Capitol Records, West was ultimately denied an artist deal.

Yonten Gyatso, the fourth Dalai Lama, was granted the title "Master of Vajradhara" by the Wanli Emperor in 1616. That same year, the Emperor invited Yonten Gyatso to visit Beijing. However, Yonten Gyatso, like his predecessor, passed away before he could make the journey.

The Hudson River flows through the Hudson Valley into New York Bay. Between New York City and Troy, New York, the river is an estuary. The Hudson River separates the city from the U.S. state of New Jersey. The East River—a tidal strait—flows from Long Island Sound and separates the Bronx and Manhattan from Long Island. The Harlem River, another tidal strait between the East and Hudson Rivers, separates most of Manhattan from the Bronx. The Bronx River, which flows through the Bronx and Westchester County, is the only entirely fresh water river in the city.

Set several hundred years after the events of Ocarina of Time and Majora’s Mask, Twilight Princess opens with Link, a young man employed as a ranch hand in Ordon Village. The peace of the village is shattered when Bulblins launch an attack, kidnapping the local children. Link gives chase but is stopped by a mysterious barrier of Twilight. Dragged into the Twilight Realm by a Shadow Beast, Link is transformed into a wolf and locked away. He is soon released by Midna, a mischievous creature from the Twilight who, despite her initial disdain for Link, offers her assistance on the condition that he follows her commands. Midna leads Link to Princess Zelda, who reveals that Zant, the ruler of the Twilight, has seized the light from three out of four Light Spirits and taken control of Hyrule. To rescue Hyrule, Link must first restore each Light Spirit by venturing into the Twilight-shrouded regions and, in his wolf form, retrieving the lost light. This is accomplished by collecting numerous "Tears of Light" scattered throughout each area. Once all the Tears of Light in a region are gathered, the corresponding Light Spirit is revived, and Link regains his human form.

During the late 20th century, New York City experienced significant economic and social changes. The city faced major economic challenges and a surge in crime as a result of widespread job losses linked to shifts in the industrial sector. Although the financial industry experienced a revival in the 1980s that significantly boosted the city's economy, crime rates continued to climb throughout that decade and into the early 1990s. It was not until the mid-1990s that crime began to decline sharply, a change attributed to updated policing methods, better economic prospects, gentrification, and an influx of new residents, including both domestic migrants and immigrants from Asia and Latin America. The 1990s also saw the rise of new economic sectors in New York, such as Silicon Alley. The city’s population reached record levels in the 2000 Census and set another new peak in the 2010 Census.

Following his high school graduation, Kanye West was awarded a scholarship to the American Academy of Art in Chicago in 1997, where he initially enrolled in painting courses. Not long after, he transferred to Chicago State University, focusing his studies on English. However, he soon found that balancing his academic workload with his passion for music was challenging. At the age of 20, Kanye made the decision to leave college in order to dedicate himself fully to his music career. This choice was met with disappointment from his mother, a professor at the same university. She later reflected, "I was always taught that college was the key to a successful life... but not every career requires a degree. For Kanye, pursuing his path in music was more about having the courage to be true to himself than simply following the conventional route."

New York City experiences an annual precipitation total of 1,270 millimeters (49.9 inches), with rainfall distributed relatively evenly throughout the year. The average snowfall during winter months, calculated from 1981 to 2010, is 66 centimeters (25.8 inches), though this amount can fluctuate significantly from one year to the next. While hurricanes and tropical storms seldom affect the New York region, they do occasionally occur and always pose a threat. On October 29, 2012, Hurricane Sandy struck New York City, unleashing a powerful storm surge that inundated streets, tunnels, and subway lines in Lower Manhattan and other neighborhoods, and caused widespread power outages across the city and its surrounding areas. The devastation caused by Sandy has led to ongoing discussions about building seawalls and other protective coastal structures along the city’s shoreline and throughout the metropolitan region to reduce the risk of similar disasters in the future.

New York City covers a total area of 468.9 square miles (1,214 km²), with 164.1 square miles (425 km²) of this area made up of water. The city's highest elevation is Todt Hill, which rises to 409.8 feet (124.9 meters) above sea level. The summit area is largely forested and forms part of a major greenbelt.

New York serves as the leading hub for political fundraising in the United States, with Manhattan home to four out of the five ZIP codes contributing the largest sums to political campaigns nationwide. The ZIP code 10021, located on the Upper East Side, accounted for the highest amount of donations to both George W. Bush and John Kerry during the 2004 presidential election. There is a significant disparity in the financial relationship between the city and both state and federal governments. For every dollar New York City pays in federal taxes, it gets back only 83 cents in services, resulting in the city sending $11.4 billion more to the federal government each year than it receives. Additionally, New York City contributes $11 billion more annually to the state government than it gets in return.

New York City is known for its lively food culture, influenced by a wide range of communities. Foods such as bagels, cheesecake, and pizza have become staples, and today, a variety of eateries—including Asian restaurants, sandwich shops, diners, and coffeehouses—are spread across the city. There are about 4,000 mobile food vendors, many operated by immigrants, offering popular street foods. According to Michelin, the city has close to one thousand notable fine dining establishments. The New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene oversees the inspection of the city’s 24,000 restaurants and assigns letter grades based on their evaluations.

Located in the borough of Manhattan, Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts serves as the focal point of Lincoln Square, situated on the Upper West Side. This renowned complex hosts several major cultural institutions, such as the Metropolitan Opera, New York City Opera, New York Philharmonic, New York City Ballet, the Vivian Beaumont Theater, the Juilliard School, Jazz at Lincoln Center, and Alice Tully Hall. The Lee Strasberg Theatre and Film Institute can be found in Union Square, and the Tisch School of the Arts is part of New York University. Additionally, Central Park SummerStage offers complimentary theater and musical performances within Central Park.

Chopin’s reputation as a virtuoso diminished over time, and he found himself teaching fewer students. Amidst the challenges of the period, he gave his final concert in Paris with cellist Auguste Franchomme, where they performed selections from the Cello Sonata Op. 65.

The United States Open Tennis Championships, recognized as one of the four Grand Slam tournaments worldwide, takes place annually at the National Tennis Center, located in Flushing Meadows-Corona Park in Queens. The New York Marathon ranks among the largest marathons globally, with the 2004, 2005, and 2006 races holding the records for the highest numbers of finishers; in 2006 alone, 37,866 runners completed the event. The Millrose Games, an annual track and field competition, is known for featuring the Wanamaker Mile as its signature race. Boxing maintains a strong presence in New York City’s sports culture, highlighted by the annual Amateur Boxing Golden Gloves tournament, which is held at Madison Square Garden. The city is closely associated with the Belmont Stakes, the oldest, longest, and final race of the Triple Crown series, which takes place at Belmont Park just outside the city limits, typically on the first or second Sunday in June. Additionally, New York City has hosted major golf tournaments, including the 1932 U.S. Open and the PGA Championships in 1930 and 1939, most notably at the nearby Winged Foot Golf Club.

The headquarters of the New York City Fire Department is located at 9 MetroTech Center. The department’s Fire Academy, where training takes place, is situated on Randalls Island. The Bureau of Fire Communications operates three separate alarm offices responsible for receiving and dispatching alarms to the correct units. The office at 11 MetroTech Center in Brooklyn manages fire communications for Manhattan/Citywide, Brooklyn, and Staten Island. Meanwhile, the alarm offices serving the Bronx and Queens are housed in different locations.

As of 2014, New York City had an estimated population of 8,491,079, marking a record high. Since the 2010 United States Census, the city has experienced a net increase in residents, with more people moving in than leaving. Between April 2010 and July 2014, New York City added 316,000 inhabitants, the largest growth among all U.S. cities during that period. The city’s population is more than double that of the next largest U.S. city, even though New York City occupies a smaller geographic area. Approximately 40% of New York State’s residents live in New York City, and the city’s population also represents a similar proportion of the total population in the New York metropolitan region.

Beginning in 2007, several major airlines became the first to sign agreements to add iPod seat connections to their aircraft. This service allows passengers to charge their iPods and access their music and video libraries through the personal seat-back screens. KLM and Air France were initially mentioned as possible participants in Apple’s initiative, but later clarified that they were only considering these features and had not joined the 2007 agreement.

The dock connector enabled the iPod to connect to various accessories, which could enhance its music, video, and photo playback. While Apple offered some accessories, most are produced by third-party companies such as Belkin and Griffin. Some peripherals use their own interface, while others interact through the iPod's screen. Many significant American cultural movements originated in New York City, including the Harlem Renaissance, which was instrumental in shaping the African-American literary canon in the United States. New York was a hub for jazz music, while the 1950s saw the rise of abstract expressionism as a leading artistic style in the city. The 1970s marked the emergence of hip hop, a new musical genre that began in New York. Additionally, the city’s punk and hardcore music scenes gained prominence throughout the 1970s and 1980s. New York has also maintained a vibrant tradition of Jewish American literature.

Unlike other major American cities, New York is uniquely split between two primary US district courts, each with its own main courthouse located in a different borough. The Southern District of New York’s main courthouse is situated on Foley Square in Manhattan, and it oversees cases from multiple areas. Meanwhile, the Eastern District of New York’s main courthouse is found in Brooklyn, with its jurisdiction including several boroughs such as Staten Island. Additionally, New York is home to the US Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit and the US Court of International Trade, both of which are also located on Foley Square in Manhattan. City Hall is also found in Manhattan.

Following the conclusion of the Second Anglo-Dutch War, England acquired New Amsterdam—now known as New York—in North America, while the Dutch received control over an island in Indonesia as part of the exchange. Between 1660 and 1670, the Lenape people suffered significant population declines due to a combination of intertribal conflicts and diseases introduced through European contact. By the year 1700, only 200 Lenape remained in the region.

Go Set a Watchman, an earlier version of To Kill a Mockingbird, was released to the public amid controversy in mid-July 2015. This manuscript, completed several years before Mockingbird, is set long after the events of that novel, though it does not serve as a direct sequel. The story follows an adult Jean Louise “Scout” Finch, who returns from New York to visit her father, Atticus Finch, in Maycomb, Alabama, where she confronts the prejudice present in her hometown. The manuscript for Watchman was thought to be lost until it was reportedly found by Harper Lee’s attorney, Tonja Carter, a claim that has been the subject of much debate. Watchman features early incarnations of several characters later seen in To Kill a Mockingbird. Lee’s agent, Andrew Nurnberg, stated that Mockingbird was initially meant to be the first in a trilogy, with Watchman as the final installment and a shorter novel to connect them; however, this idea has been challenged by rare books specialist James S. Jaffe. After examining the manuscript for Lee’s lawyer, Jaffe determined that Watchman is simply another draft of To Kill a Mockingbird. Similarly, Jonathan Mahler described Watchman as merely the initial draft of Mockingbird, and the significant overlap between the texts, sometimes even identical passages, further undermines the trilogy claim.

New York—often called New York City or the City of New York to distinguish it from the State of New York, of which it is a part—is the most populous city in the United States and the center of the New York metropolitan area, the premier gateway for legal immigration to the United States and one of the most populous urban agglomerations in the world. A global power city, New York exerts a significant impact upon commerce, finance, media, art, fashion, research, technology, education, and entertainment, its fast pace defining the term New York minute. Home to the headquarters of the United Nations, New York is an important center for international diplomacy and has been described as the cultural and financial capital of the world.

According to the Köppen climate classification system, New York City is characterized by a humid subtropical climate (Cfa) when applying the 0 °C (32 °F) isotherm for its coldest month, which is January. The city is the northernmost major city in North America with this classification. The surrounding suburbs are located in a transitional climate area. On average, New York experiences sunshine on more than half of the days each year, receiving about 57% of the possible sunlight annually. The city is designated as USDA Plant Hardiness Zone 7b.
